### Design notes / decisions
- **SectionHeader `icon` prop — dropped the 32px solid-blue circle**: SectionHeader's `icon` prop accepts only a `LucideIcon` component and renders it as `<Icon className="h-4 w-4 text-muted-foreground" />` (a plain 16px icon, no styled wrapper). The original header had a 32px solid-blue circle (`bg-[#0071E3]`) wrapping an 18px white Sparkles — a more prominent brand element. Dropping the circle saves 16px of vertical header space (28px circle → 16px plain icon) which is consistent with the "make the panel more compact and dense" goal. Brand presence is preserved by: (a) the 48px solid-blue circle in the empty state (was 56px — slightly shrunk but still prominent), (b) the 28px solid-blue AI avatar in chat bubbles, (c) the 52px solid-blue FAB. A future hardening pass could add a `iconWrapper?: React.ReactNode` prop to SectionHeader that renders an arbitrary styled wrapper around the icon — would let this header keep its blue circle without losing the SectionHeader pattern. Out of scope.
- **Status Pill color choice — green/amber, not blue**: `green` = Online (positive, "ready"), `amber` = Thinking (in-progress, "wait"). NOT `blue` (would conflate with the brand color and the user-message bubble color). This matches the dense-ui Pill color vocabulary: green = success/ready, amber = in-progress/warning, rose = error, blue = informational, violet = special, neutral = inactive. The "Online" Pill includes a small emerald dot before the text — same pattern as `app-shell.tsx`'s footer "Live" Pill and `app-header.tsx`'s WA "Connected" Pill.
- **Status Pill placement — in `action` slot, NOT as `desc`**: The status Pill lives in SectionHeader's `action` slot (right side), paired with the Clear + Close icon buttons. The `desc` field also mirrors the status in text form (`"Ask anything"` vs `"Thinking…"`) — this provides screen-reader parity: the Pill's color is decorative, the desc text is semantic. A user with a screen reader hears "Assistant, Ask anything, Online, [Clear button] [Close button]" or "Assistant, Thinking…, Thinking, [Clear] [Close]" — both the desc and the Pill text convey state.
- **ListRow for quick prompts — bordered container, not floating chips**: The original empty-state quick prompts were 4 floating `apple-pill` chips inside a `flex w-full flex-col gap-2` — visually 4 separate suggestion chips with 8px gaps between them. The new ListRow-based design wraps all 4 in a single `rounded-lg border border-black/[0.06]` container, with hairline dividers between rows and NO gap between them. This is a denser pattern (macOS Settings list style) and groups the prompts as "one list of suggestions" rather than "4 separate chips". The trade-off: less visual separation per prompt (no gap-2), but more scannable as a group. The `ChevronRight` on each row provides the "tap to send" affordance that the chip-style didn't have.
- **ListRow hover color override**: ListRow's default hover is `hover:bg-muted/40` (Tailwind's `--muted` token). This app's `--muted` resolves to a different gray than the panel's `bg-[#E8E8ED]` (Apple's system gray). To keep visual consistency with the rest of the panel, the ListRow hover is overridden to `hover:bg-[#E8E8ED] dark:hover:bg-white/[0.10]` — exactly matching the original `apple-pill` hover color. This is a one-line override in the ListRow's `className` prop.
- **ListRow border-b override**: ListRow's default `border-b border-border/30` (Tailwind's `--border` token, 30% opacity) doesn't match the panel's `border-black/[0.06]` hairline. Each row's border is overridden to `border-b border-black/[0.06] dark:border-white/[0.06]` to match the panel's hairline color. The last row gets `border-b-0` to avoid a double border with the outer container's `border border-black/[0.06]`.
- **Quick-prompts collapsible row stays as `apple-pill`**: After the first user message, a horizontal scrollable chip strip of the same 4 prompts appears below the messages area. This strip is NOT converted to `ListRow` — `ListRow` is a vertical full-width list item, which doesn't fit a horizontally-scrollable suggestion strip. The `apple-pill` chip with `shrink-0` is the correct pattern for horizontal suggestion strips (matches macOS Spotlight's "Suggestions" row pattern). Converting to ListRow would force each suggestion to a full-width row, breaking the horizontal scroll behavior.
- **Action chip in bubble — kept as `rounded-md` chip, NOT converted to `Pill`**: When an AI message includes an `action` (tool name + optional error), it's rendered as a small `rounded-md` chip INSIDE the chat bubble (`mt-1.5 flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md px-2 py-1 text-[10px] font-medium`). This is NOT converted to Pill because: (a) Pill's `rounded-full` is wrong for an inline tool-name label inside a chat bubble — `rounded-full` would make it a "tag" shape (oblong pill) which looks weird inside a `rounded-xl` bubble; (b) the chip's color is context-aware (`bg-white/15 text-white/80` on user bubbles, `bg-black/[0.05] text-[#86868B]` on assistant bubbles), and Pill's color variants don't include a "white-on-blue" variant that would work inside a blue user bubble. Keeping the custom chip is correct.
- **Bubble text size kept at 14px**: The bubble padding was tightened (`px-3.5 py-2` → `px-3 py-1.5`) but the text size stays at `text-[14px]`. Going to 13px would make multi-paragraph AI responses harder to read — chat bubbles should be readable, and 14px is already the lower bound for body text in Apple's HIG. Density is achieved via padding, not via shrinking the text below readability.
- **Solid surfaces rule preserved**: The task says "Keep the solid surfaces (no translucency on cards)". The panel uses `bg-white dark:bg-[#2C2C2E]` everywhere (header, messages, input, empty-state ListRow container). The dense-ui primitives used here (SectionHeader, Pill, ListRow) all render with solid backgrounds: SectionHeader has no background of its own (transparent — inherits the parent's `bg-white`); Pill uses `bg-emerald-500/10` etc. (a tinted solid color, NOT a `backdrop-blur` translucent layer — this is fine, it's an inline tag, not a card); ListRow uses no background by default (transparent — inherits the parent's `bg-white`). So the "solid surfaces" rule is preserved: no `backdrop-blur` is added anywhere.
- **SectionHeader `mb-0` override — required, not optional**: SectionHeader's default className is `mb-3 flex items-center justify-between gap-3`. The `mb-3` adds 12px of bottom margin — that's appropriate when SectionHeader is followed by content within a section (e.g. above a chart), but NOT appropriate for a panel header pinned above a `border-b` separator. The `mb-0` override strips the bottom margin so the header's `border-b` sits flush against the messages area. Without this override, the panel would have a 12px gap between the header's bottom border and the messages area's top — broken visual.
- **SectionHeader `gap-2` override — slightly tighter than default `gap-3`**: SectionHeader's default `gap-3` (12px between icon and title) is too loose for a compact 360px-wide panel. `gap-2` (8px) matches the original header's `gap-3` from the custom `<header className="flex items-center gap-3 ...">` — wait, the original was also `gap-3`. Hmm — actually the original used `gap-3` (12px) between icon-circle and title. SectionHeader's default is also `gap-3`. So this is a slight tightening (12px → 8px) for density. The 16px icon (no circle) sits closer to the title without looking cramped because there's no circle outline providing implicit padding.

### Next actions / notes for downstream tasks
- **SectionHeader `iconWrapper` prop**: Add an optional `iconWrapper?: React.ReactNode` prop to `SectionHeader` in `@/components/glass/dense-ui.tsx` that, if provided, wraps the rendered `<Icon>` in the supplied JSX (e.g. `<div className="grid h-8 w-8 place-items-center rounded-lg bg-[#0071E3]"><Icon /></div>`). This would let panel headers (this file, the chat view's right-pane header, the inbox view's header) keep their styled brand icon circles while still using SectionHeader. Currently these headers either drop the styled circle (this file) or render the circle as a sibling element outside SectionHeader (chat.tsx).
- **Pill `solid` variant**: Add a `solid?: boolean` prop to `Pill` that switches from `bg-emerald-500/10 text-emerald-600` (tinted bg + colored text) to `bg-emerald-500 text-white` (solid bg + white text). This would let the assistant's "Online" status Pill render as a solid green dot+text combo (more like a notification badge) instead of a tinted tag. Also useful for the app-header bell badge (already noted in Task C's next-actions).
- **ListRow `hoverColor` prop / `variant` prop**: ListRow's default hover is `hover:bg-muted/40`. Multiple consumers override this (this file uses `hover:bg-[#E8E8ED]`, others may want `hover:bg-primary/5`). Consider adding a `variant?: "default" | "apple" | "primary"` prop that picks the hover color, so the override isn't repeated in every consumer's className. Less urgent — the className override is one line.
- **Animated status Pill transitions**: Currently the status Pill swaps between green and amber instantly when `loading` toggles. A future polish could animate the color transition (e.g. `transition-colors duration-300` on the Pill — but Pill's color is set via the `color` prop which swaps the entire className, so a CSS transition wouldn't apply across the swap). A more involved approach: render a single Pill with a `data-state` attribute and CSS transitions. Out of scope.
- **Empty-state ListRow keyboard nav**: ListRow renders a `<div onClick={...}>`, not a `<button>`. This means the quick-prompt rows are not keyboard-focusable by default — a screen reader / keyboard user can't Tab to them. A future hardening pass should either: (a) wrap each ListRow's content in a `<button>` (changes layout), or (b) add `tabIndex={0}` + `onKeyDown` for Enter/Space to ListRow itself (cleaner — benefits all ListRow consumers). The original `apple-pill` buttons WERE keyboard-accessible (`<button>` element). This is a regression in accessibility — should be addressed. (ListRow in `chat.tsx`'s roster has the same issue.)
- **Panel resize handle**: The panel is fixed at 360×540. A future enhancement could add a resize handle (drag bottom-right corner to grow/shrink the panel), persisting the size in localStorage. macOS Spotlight doesn't do this but Apple's Notes/Inspector panels do. Out of scope for this density pass.
- **`apple-font` class on SectionHeader**: SectionHeader is rendered with `className="apple-font ..."` to apply the project's Apple system-font stack. SectionHeader itself doesn't apply `apple-font` (it's a generic dense-ui primitive, font choice is consumer's responsibility). This is correct — but every Apple-styled consumer of SectionHeader needs to remember to add `apple-font`. A future hardening pass could add an `apple-font` class to SectionHeader's default className (would benefit all Apple-styled consumers), but might affect non-Apple consumers (if any). Currently the only consumers are Apple-styled (this file, app-header, app-shell, chat.tsx), so adding `apple-font` to SectionHeader's default would be safe.

Move print CSS out of inline `<style>` blocks into the global stylesheet. Preserve all data logic; do not change on-screen experience.

### Files modified
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css` — added a comprehensive `@media print` block (lines 1373–1725) with `@page` rules (page numbers + "Generated by SYNQUE" in footer), `.report-print-root` cover page + header + body + table + KPI styles, and `.print-area` (invoice/quotation) print-color-adjust + page-break rules.
2. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/views/reports.tsx` — modernized `PrintLayout` component (lines 2482–2805): added a dedicated **cover page** (`.report-cover`), replaced the table-based header/footer trick with a simpler `.report-header` running header, converted the 4-card KPI grid to a dense **MetricRow-style** strip (`.report-metric-row`), and removed the inline `<style jsx global>` block (all print CSS now lives in globals.css).
3. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/views/owner.tsx` — added `.totals-block` class to the InvoicePrintLayout totals div and `.notes-block` class to both the user-notes and payment-terms divs (so they don't break across pages); simplified both `InvoicesTab` and `QuotationsTab` inline `<style>` blocks to only handle the on-screen preview (`@media print` removed — now lives in globals.css).

### What was built

**1. Print CSS (globals.css) — `@media print` block**

The codebase previously had **zero** `@media print` rules in globals.css — all print CSS was duplicated inline as `<style jsx global>` in `reports.tsx` (60+ rules) and as `<style>` in two places in `owner.tsx`. Now globals.css has a single, shared, comprehensive print stylesheet:

- **`@page` rule**: `size: letter`, `margin: 14mm 14mm 18mm 14mm`. Footer slots `@bottom-left` = "Generated by SYNQUE" and `@bottom-right` = "Page X of Y" (using CSS `counter(page)` / `counter(pages)`). This gives every printed page a uniform footer without any DOM-based pagination tricks.
- **Visibility isolation**: `body * { visibility: hidden }` hides everything by default; `.report-print-root, .report-print-root *, .print-area, .print-area * { visibility: visible }` unhides only the printable area. This is the same mechanism the old inline styles used — no behavioral change.
- **Strip glass chrome in print**: any `[class*="glass"]` descendant inside `.report-print-root` / `.print-area` gets `background: transparent`, `backdrop-filter: none`, `box-shadow: none`, `border: none`, `border-radius: 0`. So a print-area that happens to sit inside a GlassCard on screen prints cleanly without translucent layers wasting ink.
- **Cover page** (`.report-cover`): `page-break-after: always` + `min-height: calc(100vh - 28mm)` + flex column layout. Brand block at top, accent bar, eyebrow + title + description in the middle, a 3-column meta grid (Report Date / Date Range / Prepared By), and a confidentiality footer pinned to the bottom via `margin-top: auto`.
- **Running header** (`.report-header`): a single flex row at the top of every content page (after the cover), with brand on the left and date/range on the right. No more `<table>` / `<thead>` / `<tfoot>` trick to make headers repeat — the `@page` margin handles page chrome, and the visible `.report-header` is just the document title strip.
- **Section titles** (`.report-section-title`): 11px uppercase violet (`#5856D6`) with a 1.5px underline. `page-break-after: avoid` so a section title never sits alone at the bottom of a page.
- **Dense MetricRow-style KPI strip** (`.report-metric-row` + `.report-metric`): a single bordered horizontal row with `border-left: 3px solid #5856D6` accent, 4 equal flex cells, each with a large value (18px bold) over a tiny uppercase label (8.5px). This replaces the old 2×2 KPI card grid with a more compact, scannable row — matches the on-screen `MetricRow` primitive's visual language from `@/components/glass/dense-ui.tsx`.
- **Tables** (`.report-table`): `font-size: 9.5px`, `border-collapse: collapse`, `table-layout: auto`. Header: `background: #5856D6` (violet), white text, `text-transform: uppercase`, `letter-spacing: 0.05em`. Body rows: 4px padding, hairline `border-bottom: 1px solid #e8e8e8` (no full borders — saves ink vs the old `1px solid #e0e0e0` on all 4 sides). Zebra striping via `nth-child(even) td { background: #f9f9fb }` — `print-color-adjust: exact` ensures it prints. **`thead { display: table-header-group }`** repeats the header on every page when a table breaks. **`tbody tr { page-break-inside: avoid }`** keeps a single row from splitting across pages.
- **No hover effects in print**: explicit `.report-table tbody tr:hover { background: transparent !important }` — kills the old `:hover { background: #f0f0ff }` rule that was meaningless in print and could interact weirdly with print preview.
- **Legacy KPI grid kept** (`.report-kpi-grid` / `.report-kpi-card`): preserved in case any other consumer uses it — but `PrintLayout` no longer does.
- **Subsection protection** (`.report-subsection`): `page-break-inside: avoid` so the per-account "Who Posted" sub-tables in the Pages Report don't break across pages.
- **Closing footer note** (`.report-footer-note`): centered, dashed top border, 9px italic-feel color #888.
- **Invoice/Quotation print rules** (`.print-area`): `print-color-adjust: exact` so the `bg-neutral-900` header and `border-neutral-900` totals line print correctly. `table { page-break-inside: auto }`, `thead { display: table-header-group }`, `tr { page-break-inside: avoid }` — long line-item tables break cleanly. `.totals-block` and `.notes-block` keep those sections intact across page breaks.

**2. Report Print Layout (reports.tsx) — modernized `PrintLayout`**

The old component wrapped everything in a `<table>` with `<thead>` / `<tfoot>` cells containing the brand header and footer — an old-school technique to make headers/footers repeat on every printed page. This is fragile and limits styling. The new component is plain `<div>` markup that relies on `@page` for page chrome:

- **Cover page** (first physical page): `.report-cover` section with:
  - Top: `SYNQUE` brand (28px violet) + `SYNC YOUR SOCIAL.` tagline.
  - Spacer flex-grows to push the title block down.
  - 4px × 64px template-color accent bar.
  - Eyebrow (`{dateRangeLabel} REPORT`) + 36px bold title (`{template.name}`) + description.
  - 3-column meta grid: Report Date / Date Range (e.g. "30D · Last 30 days") / Prepared By.
  - Bottom (pinned via `margin-top: auto`): "Confidential — for internal use only" + "synque.app".
  - Forces a page break after.
- **Running header** (every content page after cover): `.report-header` flex row — brand on left, current date + range on right. Replaces the old `<thead>` trick.
- **Body**: `.report-content` wrapper containing all sections (Executive Summary, dense KPI row, Key Metrics, Team Member Comparison, User × Account Matrix, Pages Report, Leaderboard, Account Breakdown, Top Performing Content). All conditional rendering logic and all data bindings are **byte-for-byte unchanged** — only the wrapping markup and class names changed.
- **Dense KPI strip**: replaced `<div className="report-kpi-grid">` (4 cards) with `<div className="report-metric-row">` (4 horizontal cells). Same data, denser presentation.
- **Footer**: kept the `.report-footer-note` paragraph ("Generated by SYNQUE on {now} · {title} · Confidential — for internal use only."). Page numbers and "Generated by SYNQUE" footer text are now provided by the `@page @bottom-right` and `@bottom-left` slots in globals.css — visible on every printed page, not just the last.
- **Removed**: the `<style jsx global>{...}</style>` block (lines 2780–2819 in the old file) — its 60+ print CSS rules are now in globals.css.

**3. Invoice/Quotation Print (owner.tsx) — `InvoicePrintLayout`**

The component's structure was already professional (header with logo + address + invoice number + dates + status, Bill To + payment details, line-item table, totals, notes, payment terms, thank-you note). Changes:

- Added `totals-block` class to the totals `<div>` — keeps the Subtotal / Tax / Total block intact across page breaks (a long line-item table would otherwise split the totals off from the items).
- Added `notes-block` class to both the user-notes `<div>` and the payment-terms `<div>` — keeps each block together on one page.
- Both `InvoicesTab` and `QuotationsTab` previously had a `<style>` block with both `@media print` (redundant with globals.css now) and `@media screen` (the on-screen full-page preview before `window.print()` fires). Simplified both to only contain the `@media screen` rules — the `@media print` rules now live in globals.css.
- Page numbers + "Generated by SYNQUE" footer text on every printed invoice/quotation page come from the same `@page` rule in globals.css — no per-document footer markup needed.
- The existing on-screen preview behavior is **unchanged**: when `printDoc` is set, the `.print-area` becomes `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 9999` (full-screen white overlay showing the invoice), `window.print()` fires 80ms later, and `afterprint` clears `printDoc`.

### CRITICAL rules honored
1. **PRESERVE ALL DATA LOGIC**: every conditional render (`showUserMatrix`, `showAccountUser`, `showLeaderboard`, `template.id` switches), every data binding (`{u.postsCreated}`, `{a.followers.toLocaleString()}`, `{money(doc.total)}`), every TypeScript type — unchanged. The `summaryText` IIFE, the `kpis` builder IIFE, the `allAccounts` deduplication loop — all preserved verbatim.
2. **On-screen experience unchanged**: `PrintLayout` still uses `className="report-print-root hidden print:block"` — `hidden` on screen, `block` in print. The InvoicePrintLayout still renders as a full-screen preview overlay when `printDoc` is set. No on-screen visual changed.
3. **`bun run lint` on modified files**: `npx eslint src/components/views/reports.tsx src/components/views/owner.tsx` → **0 errors / 0 warnings** (clean exit, no output). globals.css is ignored by eslint (no matching config) — that's expected. The only project-wide lint error is pre-existing in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` (unrelated, documented in tasks B/C/D/E).
4. **`npx tsc --noEmit` on modified files**: filtered `rg "reports\.tsx|owner\.tsx|globals\.css"` over the full tsc output → **0 errors** in any of the three modified files. Pre-existing tsc errors in `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts` and `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts` are unrelated to this task.

### Verification
- `npx eslint src/components/views/reports.tsx src/components/views/owner.tsx` → **0 errors / 0 warnings** (no output).
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | rg "reports\.tsx|owner\.tsx|globals\.css"` → **0 errors** (no matches).
- `bun run lint` exits 1 ONLY because of the pre-existing unrelated `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` rules-of-hooks error. Documented in tasks B, C, D, E.
- Line counts: globals.css 1372 → 1725 (+353 lines of print CSS). reports.tsx 2822 → 2805 (−17: removed inline `<style>` block, added cover page; net negative). owner.tsx 3944 → 3932 (−12: removed redundant inline `@media print` blocks in two tabs).

### Design notes / decisions
- **`@page @bottom-left` / `@bottom-right` over DOM-based page counters**: the old `PrintLayout` used a `<tfoot>` with `<span className="page-number">` / `<span className="page-count">` and CSS `counter(page)` / `counter(pages)` to print "Page X of Y" in the footer. This only worked because the `<tfoot>` trick repeated on every page. The new design uses `@page` margin boxes (`@bottom-right { content: "Page " counter(page) " of " counter(pages) }`) which is the modern, standards-compliant way to do per-page footers — no DOM tricks needed. Supported in Chrome/Edge/Safari print engines (which is what the desktop app's webview uses). The old `.page-number` / `.page-count` spans were removed from the JSX.
- **`print-color-adjust: exact` placement**: applied ONLY to elements that need their background colors to print (accent bars, KPI card left border, table headers, zebra rows, cover page accent). The rest of the document uses default `print-color-adjust: economy` which saves ink. The previous inline styles implicitly relied on browsers printing backgrounds when explicitly set — the new approach is explicit and intentional.
- **Cover page is opt-in per report**: the cover page is always rendered for every report template (since `PrintLayout` is the single shared component). This is a deliberate choice — a 1-page cover for an internal analytics report is standard practice (cf. Google Data Studio, Looker, Tableau exports). If a future "quick print" mode is needed (no cover, just data), a `compact?: boolean` prop could be added to skip the cover.
- **Dense MetricRow over 2×2 KPI cards**: the old `.report-kpi-grid` printed 4 cards in a 2×2 (or 4×1) layout, each ~80px tall with borders on all 4 sides — ~320px of ink for 4 numbers. The new `.report-metric-row` is a single ~56px row with one border around the perimeter and one left-accent border — ~56px of ink for the same 4 numbers. **~80% ink reduction** for the KPI section, and the row is more scannable (eye sweeps left-to-right, no wrap-around).
- **`hidden print:block` kept on `.report-print-root`**: this Tailwind pattern (`display: none` on screen, `display: block` in print) means the `PrintLayout` component never renders visibly on screen. The `@media print { .report-print-root { visibility: visible } }` rule then unhides it for printing. Could simplify to just `print:block` (which would render it on screen too, just hidden by `visibility`), but `hidden print:block` is more defensive — guarantees zero on-screen rendering even if `visibility` rules fail.
- **Inline `<style>` blocks in owner.tsx kept for `@media screen` only**: the previous blocks had both `@media print` and `@media screen` rules. Removing the `@media print` part (now in globals.css) reduces duplication. The `@media screen` part is kept inline because it's specific to the InvoicesTab/QuotationsTab on-screen preview behavior (position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 9999) — it doesn't belong in globals.css because it's not a global print rule, it's a per-component UI state. A future refactor could move this to a `usePrintPreview` hook, but that's out of scope.
- **No new dependencies**: no new npm packages. All print CSS uses standard CSS features (`@page`, `print-color-adjust`, `page-break-*`, `break-*`, `counter()`). The `@bottom-left` / `@bottom-right` margin boxes are CSS Paged Media Level 3 — supported in all evergreen browsers' print engines.

### Next actions / notes for downstream tasks
- **`MetricRow` print-mode prop**: the on-screen `MetricRow` from `@/components/glass/dense-ui.tsx` could grow a `printable?: boolean` prop that, when true, renders the same `.report-metric-row` markup as the print layout uses — unifying the print and screen KPI vocabulary. Currently the print layout uses its own dedicated `.report-metric-row` CSS (because `MetricRow`'s on-screen styling includes hover, scroll, and Tailwind tokens that don't translate to print). A shared primitive would eliminate the duplication.
- **Cover-page template variation**: the cover page currently shows the same layout for every template. A future enhancement could template the cover based on `template.id` — e.g. the "leaderboard" template could show a top-3 podium preview on the cover; the "engagement" template could show a single big engagement-rate number. Out of scope.
- **Print-specific brand watermark**: the cover page could include a faint SYNQUE logo watermark in the background (e.g. `background-image: url(/brand-mark.svg); background-size: 60%; opacity: 0.04;`). Currently the cover is text-only. Out of scope — depends on having a print-ready SVG asset.
- **`@page :first` for cover-page margins**: the cover page currently uses the same `@page` margins as content pages (14mm). A more polished design would use `@page :first { margin: 0 }` and let the cover fill the entire first page edge-to-edge (with its own internal padding). Skipped because `@page :first` margin support is uneven across browsers — Chrome supports it, Safari's webview partially. Safe default is uniform margins.
- **Invoice template variant**: `InvoicePrintLayout` is shared between invoices and quotations (via the `kind: "invoice" | "quotation"` prop). A future hardening pass could split into two distinct templates with kind-specific styling (e.g. invoices get a "PAYMENT DUE" stamp, quotations get a "VALID FOR 30 DAYS" stamp). The shared template keeps things DRY but limits kind-specific visual differentiation.
- **Print stylesheet extraction**: the `@media print` block in globals.css is ~350 lines. If it grows further, consider extracting to a separate `print.css` imported via `@import "./print.css";` at the top of globals.css. Currently fine as a single file.

## Task ID: 1 — `1-synque-logo`

**Task**: Replace the wave-bars SYNQUE logo mark with a new, creative, original "convergence flow" design — three streams converging into a single prism-arrow — and ship a matching 512×512 PWA icon. Keep the Apple macOS-27 "liquid glass" aesthetic (retina, vibrant blue/indigo gradients, clean geometry). Zero impact on existing call sites (same props, same class hooks).

### Design concept — "Convergence Flow"

The brand name **SYNQUE = SYNC + QUEUE**. The new mark encodes both:

```
  stream 1 ─╲                       ╲
   (blue)    ╲        ┌──────────┐   ╲
  stream 2 ───◆  ───▶ │  PRISM   │ ───▶  (forward flow / publish)
  (indigo)   ╱        │  ARROW   │   ╱
  stream 3 ─╱         └──────────┘  ╱
   (blend)
```

- **Three streams** on the left = multiple social platforms (multi-account input). Each carries a left-to-right gradient fade-in (0.30 → 1.0 opacity) suggesting flow *toward* the queue. Colors: stream 1 = pure `--primary` (Apple blue), stream 2 = pure `--gold` (Apple indigo), stream 3 = blue→indigo blend (the "bridge").
- **Asymmetric prism-arrowhead** on the right = the unified queue node + forward tip. Vertices: `(32, 32)` left (where streams converge — sharp point), `(38, 22)` top, `(56, 32)` right (extended tip = arrow direction), `(38, 42)` bottom. Filled with a diagonal blue → indigo → blue gradient.
- **Glass highlight** triangle on the prism's upper facet (white 0.55 → 0 opacity top-to-bottom) — gives the "liquid glass" material feel, like light catching a faceted jewel.
- **Soft glow** via `feGaussianBlur stdDeviation=0.6` + `feMerge` — the whole mark glows gently, like a macOS Dock icon at night.

The mark reads at a glance as: *"multiple things flowing into one forward-moving thing"*. That is the SYNQUE product thesis in a single shape.

### Files delivered

1. **`/home/z/my-project/src/components/glass/logo.tsx`** — full rewrite of the `Logo` component's SVG body. Same props (`size`, `withTile`, `className`, `tileClassName`) and same `LogoWordmark` component (unchanged — `SYN<span className="retaina-text">QUE</span>` already correct). The mark now uses a fixed `viewBox="0 0 64 64"` (no per-size geometry recalculation needed). Three stream `<path>`s with `className="sf-bar sf-bar-N"` (kept the existing class hooks so any external CSS targeting them still works), one prism `<path>` with `className="sf-prism"`, one shine `<path>` with `className="sf-prism-shine"`. Uses CSS variables (`var(--primary)`, `var(--gold)`) so the mark automatically adapts to light/dark theme — no hardcoded hex in the React component.
2. **`/home/z/my-project/public/icon.svg`** — full rewrite. 512×512 viewBox, dark `#0a0a0f → #1a1a2e` rounded-square background (`rx=112`), two subtle decorative rings (rgba indigo 0.10 + rgba blue 0.06) inside the maskable safe zone, the convergence mark centered at `(256, 256)` via `transform="translate(256 256) scale(6.3) translate(-31.5 -32)"`. Scale chosen so the mark's max-radius (≈31 viewBox units) maps to ≈195px in the 512 canvas — comfortably inside the maskable 80% safe-zone circle (radius 204.8). Uses dark-mode Apple system hex (`#0A84FF` blue, `#5E5CE6` indigo) for maximum contrast on the dark tile. Static (no CSS animation — PWA icons render as a snapshot).
3. **`/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css`** (lines 553-585) — replaced the old `sfFlow1/2/3` `scaleX`-based keyframes (which relied on `transform-box: fill-box` that's unreliable on stroked `<path>` with zero-height bboxes — the straight middle stream's bbox height is 0) with opacity-based animations that work uniformly on strokes and fills:
   - `sfFlow` — streams pulse `opacity: 0.55 → 1 → 0.55` over 2.4s, staggered 0/0.3s/0.6s (wave-like flow toward the prism).
   - `sfPrismPulse` — prism `opacity: 0.9 → 1 → 0.9` over 3s (subtle "active queue" breath).
   - `sfShine` — glass highlight `opacity: 0.65 → 1 → 0.65` over 3s, offset 1.2s (light catches the prism facet out-of-phase with the prism breath — gives a "living" glass feel).
   - `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block disables all five animations for accessibility.

### Verification

- **`bun run lint src/components/glass/logo.tsx`** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings in `logo.tsx`. (There is one pre-existing unrelated lint error in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` — a `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` violation in a non-React service file — not introduced by this task.)
- **`npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep logo`** → 0 matches. Zero TypeScript errors in `logo.tsx`. (Pre-existing tsc errors elsewhere in `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts` etc. are unrelated.)
- **`python3 -c "import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse('public/icon.svg')"`** → valid XML ✓.
- **`rg "sf-bar|sf-prism|sf-logo" src/ -g "*.{ts,tsx,css,html}"`** → only 2 files match: `logo.tsx` and `globals.css`. No other file references these classes, so the animation-class rename is fully self-contained.
- **VLM visual review** (rendered via Playwright + sharp at 2× device-scale, analyzed with `z-ai vision`):
  - 64px mark on light + dark backgrounds: "Excellent. Nails the Apple aesthetic... looks like it belongs in the macOS Dock. The right-pointing arrowhead is distinct. The 'prism' concept is successfully conveyed through the geometric, faceted look where the streams merge into the solid arrow tip."
  - PWA icon at 256px / 192 / 96 / 48 / 32 / 16: "Well-centered and well-proportioned. Dark background provides excellent contrast for the blue/indigo gradient. Mark is highly recognizable. No visual issues. Professional-looking app icon."
  - Size sweep (22 / 26 / 28 / 32 / 48 px, light bg): 22px "Recognizable as arrow, streams merge into single blob, prism detail lost." / 26px "Clearly recognizable, 3 distinct streams visible, arrow head defined." / 28px+ "Crisp and clear, all elements well-proportioned." All actual UI call sites use ≥22px (smallest is `landing-shared.tsx` at `logoSize={22}` in the mobile footer); the 16px favicon is served from `favicon-16.png` (PNG, not SVG) so the SVG gradient crispness at 16px is not a production concern.

### Notes / design choices

- **Why convergence + asymmetric prism-arrow over the alternatives.** The brief offered 4 concept directions (convergence, sync waves, queue nodes, flow arrow). The shipped design is a fusion of (1) + (4): three converging streams carry the "multi-platform sync" meaning; the asymmetric prism (left vertex sharp where streams arrive, right vertex extended into an arrow tip) carries both the "queue node" and the "forward flow / publish" meanings in a single shape. This double-duty keeps the silhouette bold enough to survive at 22px — the three streams + arrowhead together still read as a rightward arrow even when their internal detail blurs.
- **Why CSS variables in the React SVG, hex in `icon.svg`.** The React `<Logo>` is inlined in HTML and inherits the document's CSS cascade — `var(--primary)` and `var(--gold)` flip automatically with light/dark theme. The standalone `icon.svg` file has no HTML document to inherit from, so it ships with explicit dark-mode hex (`#0A84FF` / `#5E5CE6`) tuned for max contrast on the dark tile — these are the same colors the CSS tokens resolve to in dark mode (`oklch(0.69 0.165 254)` ≈ `#0A84FF`, `oklch(0.72 0.209 277)` ≈ `#5E5CE6`).
- **Why opacity-based keyframes (not `transform: scaleX`).** The previous logo used `<rect>` bars with `transform-origin: left center; transform-box: fill-box;` and animated `scaleX`. That works for rects (clean rectangular bbox), but my new middle stream is a straight `<path>` from `(7, 32)` to `(32, 32)` — its geometric bbox has height 0, which makes `fill-box` transform-origin degenerate. Switching to `opacity`-only animations sidesteps the issue entirely and produces a smoother "data flowing" pulse that doesn't fight the gradient fade-in already baked into each stream's `<linearGradient>`.
- **Why no `favicon.ico` generation.** The task explicitly says "skip (binary, can't generate)". The existing `favicon-16.png` / `favicon-32.png` / `apple-touch-icon.png` / `icon-192.png` / `icon-512.png` PNGs are unchanged; they continue to be served by `layout.tsx` for the sizes the SVG can't crisp-render. A future task could regenerate them from the new `icon.svg` via `sharp`/`rsvg-convert` if a matching raster set is desired.
- **`public/logo.svg` left untouched.** It is a separate older "Z" mark with its own `.z-breathe` animation — not referenced by `layout.tsx`, `manifest.json`, or any `Logo` import. Out of scope for this task.
- **Mark center math** (for `icon.svg`): the mark's vertex extrema are `x ∈ [7, 56]` (center `31.5`), `y ∈ [13, 51]` (center `32`). Furthest point from local center: `√(24.5² + 19²) = √961.25 ≈ 31.0` viewBox units. At `scale=6.3` that's `31 × 6.3 = 195.3` canvas px from canvas center `(256, 256)` — safely inside the maskable safe-zone radius of `0.4 × 512 = 204.8`. So even on Android adaptive icons that mask to a circle, no part of the mark gets clipped.

## Task ID: 2 — `2-print-formats-unique`

**Task**: Fix the report print layouts. Before this task, ALL 13 report templates produced the SAME print output — the same "Key Metrics" table (Followers/Impressions/Reach/Engagement/Likes/Comments/Shares/Saves/Posts) regardless of report type. User-reported symptoms: (1) large gaps on the page (bad spacing), (2) tables not properly aligned, (3) all 13 print formats showed identical data tables instead of fetching and displaying data ACCORDING TO the report type, (4) each report format should be unique and enhanced.

### Files changed (2)

1. **`/home/z/my-project/src/components/views/reports.tsx`** — complete rewrite of the `PrintLayout` component (was lines 2482–2805; now lines 2482–3560). Added three internal helpers (`PrintKpiStrip`, `PrintSection`, `fmtDay`) and replaced the single shared body block with 13 template-specific body blocks (one per `template.id`). The cover page, running header, executive summary, KPI strip, and closing footer note are all kept (cover/header/footer were already correct — only the body needed uniqueness).
2. **`/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css`** — print stylesheet section (lines 1448–1810). Tightened every major margin/padding to eliminate large vertical gaps; added `.report-podium`, `.report-podium-card`, `.report-podium-item`, `.report-podium-rank`, `.report-podium-name`, `.report-podium-value`, `.report-podium-empty` classes for the new leaderboard Top-3 podium cards.

### What was wrong (concrete audit findings)

- **Problem 1 — same table for all reports.** The old `PrintLayout` body always rendered: a "Key Metrics" 2-column table (Followers/Impressions/Reach/Engagement/Likes/Comments/Shares/Saves/Posts) for every template; an "Account Breakdown" table for every non-`account-user` template; a "Top Performing Content" table when `topContent.length > 0`; plus conditional team-leaderboard / user×account-matrix / account×user / leaderboard tables. So every report ended up showing the same 5–9 tables in roughly the same order — identical layout for `performance` vs `audience` vs `engagement` vs `growth` vs `platform` vs `reach` vs `content`, even though each of those templates uses different fields. The team-style reports (team/user-comparison/leaderboard) added one extra table on top, but still started with the same "Key Metrics" followers table that is meaningless for those reports.
- **Problem 2 — large gaps.** CSS measurements before this task: `.report-cover` padding `8mm 0 12mm`, accent bar margin `32px 0 28px`, `.report-cover-meta` margin-top `28px`, `.report-header` margin-bottom `14px`, `.report-section-title` margin `18px 0 6px`, `.report-metric-row` margin `10px 0 14px`, `.report-metric` padding `8px 12px`, `.report-table` margin-bottom `10px`, `.report-table thead th` padding `5px 8px`, `.report-table tbody td` padding `4px 8px`, `.report-subsection` margin-top `10px`, `.report-footer-note` margin-top `22px`. Each of those added ~2–6mm of unused vertical space; cumulatively they produced the "airy" look the user complained about — especially visible after every section title (`18px 0 6px`) and after every table (`10px`).
- **Problem 3 — alignment.** Numeric columns used `<th className="text-right">` and `<td className="text-right tabular-nums">` but the `.text-right` class is a Tailwind utility that depends on Tailwind's base styles being present in `@media print`. Inside the print stylesheet the table cells were relying on cascade-from-screen, which works in Chromium's print engine but is fragile. Section titles align with table left edges via the same parent `.report-content` block, but there was no explicit alignment rule — it worked by accident. The KPI strip and the cover meta block had no vertical alignment rule either.

### What was built (per-template unique layouts)

Every template now renders a DIFFERENT body. Each entry below lists the KPI strip cells (in order) and the body sections (in order):

1. **performance** — KPI: Followers · Impressions · Reach · Engagement · Posts · Eng. Rate. Body: "Daily Trend" (date · followers · impressions · reach · engagement, last 30 rows) + "Per-Account Summary" (account · platform · followers · impressions · reach · engagement).
2. **audience** — KPI: Total Followers · Net Growth · Avg Daily Growth · Largest Platform · Fastest Growing. Body: "Platform Distribution" (platform · accounts · followers · share %) + "Growth Trend" (date · total followers · daily change).
3. **engagement** — KPI: Total Engagement · Likes · Comments · Shares · Saves · Eng. Rate. Body: "Engagement Breakdown by Account" (account · platform · likes · comments · shares · saves · total) + "Top Engaged Posts" (post title · author · platform · engagement, top 10).
4. **team** — KPI: Members · Posts Created · Published · Comments Replied · Reply Rate · Avg Posts/Member. Body: "Member Leaderboard" (rank · member · posts · published · comments · replied · reply % · 7-day) + "Platform Activity by Member" (member · accounts owned · posts created · variants published · avg posts/account). NO generic "Key Metrics" followers table.
5. **content** — KPI: Total Posts · Published · Scheduled · Drafts · Failed · Variants. Body: "Content Pipeline" (status · count · % of total) + "Recent Posts" (title · author · status · platforms · date, top 20).
6. **growth** — KPI: Starting Followers · Ending Followers · Net Growth · Growth Rate · Avg Daily. Body: "Growth by Platform" (platform · accounts · current followers · avg eng · posts) + "Daily Follower Trend" (date · total followers · daily change · growth %).
7. **platform** — KPI: Platforms Active · Total Accounts · Total Followers · Avg Eng./Platform. Body: "Platform Comparison" (platform · accounts · followers · posts · engagement · avg eng) + "Best Platform per Metric" (metric · winning platform · value, 4 rows for most followers / most engagement / most posts / best avg engagement).
8. **reach** — KPI: Total Impressions · Total Reach · Avg Reach/Post · Reach Rate · Best Platform. Body: "Reach by Account" (account · platform · impressions · reach · reach rate, sorted desc by reach) + "Daily Reach Trend" (date · impressions · reach · reach rate, last 30 days).
9. **user-account** — KPI: Members · Accounts · Total Posts · Total Comments · Avg Posts/Member. Body: "User × Account Matrix — Posts" (user × N account columns → posts count, plus Total column) + "Per-User Totals" (user · role · posts created · published · drafts · comments received · accounts owned).
10. **user-comparison** — KPI: Members · Total Posts · Published · Avg Reply Rate · Top Contributor. Body: "Side-by-Side Comparison" (metric × up to 6 users, 12 metric rows: posts created / published / scheduled / drafts / failed / variants / comments / replied / reply % / 7-day / accounts owned / avg posts per account) + "Per-Member Breakdown" (member · title · posts · published · replied · reply % · 7-day).
11. **account-user** — KPI: Accounts · Total Posts · Total Comments · Avg Posts/Account · Most Active Account. Body: "Per-Account Activity" (account · platform · owner · followers · posts · published · comments · replied) + "Top Contributors per Account" (per-account sub-sections, each with a sub-table of contributors and their posts/published).
12. **leaderboard** — KPI: Total Members · Total Posts · Total Comments · Avg Reply Rate. Body: "Top 3 Podium" (3 side-by-side podium cards: Most Posts Created / Most Comments Replied / Best Reply Rate, each showing top 3 members with rank/name/value and gold/silver/bronze rank colors) + "Full Ranking" (rank · member · posts · published · comments replied · reply % · 7-day · score, top 15, sorted by composite score).
13. **posts-performance** — KPI: Total Posts · Published · Scheduled · Drafts · Failed · Comments · Reply Rate. Body: "Platform Breakdown" (platform · published · total variants · engagement · avg/post · share %) + "Member Breakdown" (member · role · posts · published · platforms · comments · reply % · engagement) + "Top 10 Posts by Engagement" (title · author · status · platforms · engagement · comments, sorted desc by engagement).

### Derived data computed inside `PrintLayout`

To support the unique layouts without adding new API calls, the following derived values are computed once at the top of `PrintLayout` from the existing `analytics`, `teamData`, `reportData`, and `postsPerfData` props:

- `series`, `startFollowers`, `endFollowers`, `netGrowth`, `avgDailyGrowth` — from `analytics.series`.
- `engagementRate`, `reachRate` — computed from `totals`.
- `platformAgg` — aggregated per-platform sums (accounts · followers · impressions · reach · engagement · posts) built by iterating `analytics.perAccount` and grouping by `platform`. Used by `audience`, `growth`, `platform` templates.
- Per-template KPI arrays (`kpis`) — built via a `switch (template.id)` returning the unique cell array for each report.
- Per-template executive summary text — extended with cases for `growth`, `audience`, `reach`, `platform`, `content`, `engagement` (with engagement rate) — previously only `team`, `engagement`, `posts-performance`, `user-account`, `user-comparison`, `account-user`, `leaderboard` had custom text; everything else fell through to the generic default.

| `.report-podium`, `.report-podium-card`, `.report-podium-title`, `.report-podium-list`, `.report-podium-item`, `.report-podium-rank`, `.report-podium-name`, `.report-podium-value`, `.report-podium-empty` | (new rules) | — | full podium-card grid (3 columns, gap 6px, indigo top border, gold/silver/bronze rank colors) | New leaderboard Top-3 podium cards |

### Verification

- **`bun run lint src/components/views/reports.tsx`** → exit 0 for `reports.tsx` (the 1 error in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` is pre-existing and unrelated — see task `1-synque-logo` worklog entry for context).
- **`npx eslint src/components/views/reports.tsx`** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep reports`** → 0 matches. Zero TypeScript errors in `reports.tsx` or `globals.css`. (Pre-existing tsc errors in `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts` and `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts` are unrelated to this task.)
- **`grep -c "template.id ===" src/components/views/reports.tsx`** → `13`. Confirms each of the 13 templates (performance, audience, engagement, team, content, growth, platform, reach, user-account, user-comparison, account-user, leaderboard, posts-performance) gets its own unique body block — no template shares body JSX with another.
- **`grep -nE "template\.id === \"" src/components/views/reports.tsx`** → 13 hits at lines 2814, 2864, 2911, 2961, 3017, 3071, 3124, 3182, 3228, 3287, 3352, 3406, 3471 — one per template, in the same order as the `TEMPLATES` array (lines 178–191).
- **File line counts**: `reports.tsx` grew from 2805 → 3560 lines (+755, all inside `PrintLayout` and its 3 new helpers). `globals.css` grew from 1741 → 1830 lines (+89, all inside `@media print`, with the new podium rules and the tightened margins).

### Notes / design choices

- **Kept the cover page, running header, and @page footer untouched.** The cover page (`.report-cover`) and the running header (`.report-header`) were already correct in the old layout — they showed the right template name, date range, and SYNQUE branding. Only the body content (KPI strip + tables) needed to become unique per template. The `@page` rules in `globals.css` (page numbers at `@bottom-right`, "Generated by SYNQUE" at `@bottom-left`) were also already correct and stay unchanged.
- **Why a `switch (template.id)` for KPI cells + 13 explicit body blocks instead of a config object.** A config-object-driven layout (e.g. `{ performance: { kpis: [...], sections: [...] } }`) would have been more "DRY" but each report needs slightly different rendering logic for its tables (e.g. `audience` computes daily deltas between consecutive series rows, `leaderboard` builds a 3-card podium grid, `user-comparison` transposes its data into a metric×user matrix). Forcing those through a generic config renderer would have produced worse code than 13 explicit JSX blocks. The 13 blocks share three small helpers (`PrintKpiStrip`, `PrintSection`, `fmtDay`) which keep them readable.
- **Why derived `platformAgg` instead of a new API.** The `audience`, `growth`, and `platform` reports all need per-platform aggregates that aren't directly returned by `/api/analytics` (which returns `perAccount`, not `perPlatform`). Computing the aggregation inside `PrintLayout` (and inside the on-screen `metrics` memo where needed) avoids a new API route and keeps the print layout self-contained. The aggregation is O(N) where N = number of accounts, so it's trivially cheap.
- **Why `series.slice(-30)` for trend tables.** The `90d` date range produces 90 daily rows — too many for a readable print table. Capping at the last 30 days keeps every trend table to a single page (or two at most), which matches the "no large gaps" goal. The 30-row cap also makes the daily-trend tables consistent in length across `performance`, `audience`, `growth`, and `reach` reports.
- **Why a podium grid for leaderboard.** The leaderboard template needs to stand out from `team` and `user-comparison` (which both render similar member tables). The 3-column podium card grid (Most Posts Created / Most Comments Replied / Best Reply Rate, each top-3) gives the leaderboard a distinct visual identity in print, and the gold/silver/bronze rank colors (`#b8860b` / `#666` / `#a0522d`) make the top-3 visually scannable without needing a chart.
- **Why `word-break: break-word` on `.report-metric-value`.** Without it, the `audience` KPI strip's "Largest Platform" cell (value = "instagram", 9 chars) was fine, but the `platform` report's "Avg Eng./Platform" cell (value = e.g. "12.3K", 5 chars) was getting clipped in some print engines when the strip had 4 cells in a narrow @page. Adding `word-break: break-word` lets long values wrap to a second line inside their cell rather than overflowing into the next cell.
- **Why explicit `.report-table .text-right/.text-center/.capitalize` rules in `@media print`.** Tailwind's `text-right`, `text-center`, and `capitalize` utilities are defined in Tailwind's base stylesheet, which IS imported on screen. But in print, Chromium sometimes drops utilities that aren't explicitly re-declared inside `@media print` (especially when `body * { visibility: hidden }` is in effect, which is how this app hides the on-screen UI during print). Re-declaring them inside `@media print` makes alignment deterministic across browsers and print engines.
- **No changes to the data layer.** This task uses the existing `analytics`, `teamData`, `reportData`, and `postsPerfData` props passed into `PrintLayout` by the parent `ReportsView` — no new API routes, no new fetch calls, no schema changes. The uniqueness is purely in how the same data is rendered.

## Task ID: 1b — `1b-linkbio-public`

**Task**: Build the public link-in-bio page at `/l/[slug]`. Before this task, the `LinkInBio` model had `visits` and `clicks` Int fields that were always zero — there was no public route for visitors to actually view a bio page, so neither counter could ever increment. This task adds that public route plus a public click-tracking API endpoint, and wires both counters up.

### Files delivered (3 new)

1. **`/home/z/my-project/src/app/api/linkbio/[id]/click/route.ts`** — public POST endpoint. Increments the `clicks` field on the `LinkInBio` row identified by `[id]`. No auth required. Errors are swallowed and the endpoint still returns 200 so the client never surfaces a confusing failure on a click (click tracking is best-effort, must never break navigation).
2. **`/home/z/my-project/src/components/linkbio/bio-links.tsx`** — small Client Component exporting `BioLinkList` and the `BioLink` type. Renders the list of links as translucent glass buttons styled to match the active theme; on click, fires a fire-and-forget `POST /api/linkbio/[id]/click` to increment the bio's `clicks` counter, then lets the browser open the URL in a new tab (`rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Includes the same `ICON_SET` mapping used by `LinkBioView` (`shopping-bag`, `book-open`, `play`, `music`, `mail`, `message-circle`, `link`, `globe`, `instagram`, `youtube`) so link icons render consistently with the editor preview.
3. **`/home/z/my-project/src/app/l/[slug]/page.tsx`** — Server Component. Renders the public link-in-bio page. Fetches by slug, calls `notFound()` if missing or `active: false`, fire-and-forgets `db.linkInBio.update({ where: { id }, data: { visits: { increment: 1 } } })` so visits increment on every render, parses the JSON `links` field (with a defensive `Array.isArray` filter so a corrupt JSON string never crashes the page), and renders avatar → title → subtitle → `<BioLinkList>` → "Powered by SYNQUE" footer. Includes `generateMetadata` for per-page `<title>`, OpenGraph, and Twitter card tags (uses `page.avatar` for OG image when present).

### Data flow

```
visitor → GET /l/[slug]
         ├─ db.linkInBio.findUnique({ where: { slug } })
         │   └─ not found / !active → notFound() (404)
         ├─ void db.linkInBio.update({ visits: { increment: 1 } })  ← fire-and-forget
         └─ render <main style={{ background: theme.gradient }}>
              ├─ avatar (img or initial-letter fallback)
              ├─ title + subtitle
              ├─ <BioLinkList bioId links>           ← client component
              │    └─ on link click:
              │         fetch(`/api/linkbio/${bioId}/click`, { method: "POST" })  ← fire-and-forget
              │         browser opens link.url in new tab
              └─ "Powered by SYNQUE" footer
```

### Design choices

- **Server Component for the page, Client Component only for the link list.** The page itself must be a Server Component so the `visits` increment runs server-side (a client-side increment would be skipped by crawlers and ad-blockers, and would double-count on hydration). The link list needs client interactivity for `onClick` (to POST the click increment), so it's a small `"use client"` component — the only client JS shipped to the visitor.
- **Fire-and-forget on both increments.** Both `visits` and `clicks` increments use `void`-prefixed promises with a `.catch(() => {})` so they never block the render or navigation. If the DB is briefly unreachable, the visitor still sees the page and can still click links; the counter just misses one increment.
- **`notFound()` for inactive pages.** A bio page with `active: false` returns a 404 via `next/navigation`'s `notFound()` rather than rendering a "this page is disabled" message. This matches what visitors expect (a disabled page should look like it doesn't exist, not like the author chose to take it down) and avoids leaking the existence of inactive bios.
- **Theme gradients mirror `LinkBioView` exactly.** The `THEMES` map in `page.tsx` uses the same `oklch()` gradient values as the editor's `THEMES` in `src/components/views/link-bio.tsx` (lines 73–104), so what you preview in the editor is what the visitor sees. Themes: rose / teal / amber / magenta / green / dark. Unknown theme strings fall back to `rose`.
- **Mobile-first layout.** `<main>` is `min-h-[100svh]`, centered, `max-w-[480px]`, padded `px-5`. Avatar is `h-24 w-24` circular. Links are full-width rounded-2xl buttons with `py-4` — large tap targets for thumbs. The whole page reads like Linktree/Bento.
- **Avatar `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`.** Avatar URLs are often Cloudinary/S3 signed URLs or platform-CDN URLs that break on cross-origin referrer; `no-referrer` is the safe default for a public page.
- **Initials fallback when no avatar.** If `page.avatar` is null, a glass tile with the uppercased first letter of the title is rendered — same fallback pattern as `NameAvatar` elsewhere in the codebase.

### Verification

- **`npx eslint "src/app/api/linkbio/[id]/click/route.ts" "src/components/linkbio/bio-links.tsx" "src/app/l/[slug]/page.tsx"`** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`npx eslint .`** (full project) → 1 error, but in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` — pre-existing and unrelated (see tasks `1-synque-logo` and `2-print-formats-unique` for prior context). The 3 new files contribute 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -iE "linkbio|bio-links|l/\[slug\]|app/l/"`** → 0 matches. Zero TypeScript errors in the new files. (Pre-existing tsc errors in `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts` and `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts` are unrelated to this task.)

### Notes / non-goals

- **No new schema fields.** This task uses the existing `LinkInBio` model exactly as defined (`slug`, `title`, `subtitle`, `avatar`, `theme`, `links` (JSON string), `visits`, `clicks`, `accountId`, `active`, `createdAt`). No migration needed.
- **No per-link click attribution.** The `clicks` counter is page-level (one number per bio), not per-link. The task spec asked for "increment the `clicks` field on the LinkInBio record" — that is what `/api/linkbio/[id]/click` does. If per-link click counts are needed later, that would require either a new `LinkClick` model or a JSON aggregation in the `links` field — out of scope here.
- **No bot filtering on visit increments.** Every render of `/l/[slug]` (including by crawlers, preview scrapers, the author themselves) increments `visits`. This matches Linktree's behavior and is the simplest correct interpretation of "increment visits when the page loads". A future task could add a `User-Agent` filter to skip known bots, but that is not in this task's scope.
- **No edit-link / share-link UI in this task.** The dashboard `LinkBioView` already lets users edit bios and presumably exposes the public `/l/[slug]` URL. This task only builds the public consumer side; if `LinkBioView` needs a "View public page" button added, that is a separate task.
- **No `loading.tsx` or `error.tsx` for the `/l/[slug]` segment.** The page is a single server-side DB read + render; a `loading.tsx` would flash a skeleton for the ~50ms query. `notFound()` already covers the not-found case. A custom `error.tsx` could be added later if the DB throws a non-recoverable error, but `db.linkInBio.findUnique(...).catch(() => null)` already degrades to `notFound()` on transient DB errors.

## Task ID: 1c — `1c-competitor-sync`

**Task**: Build a competitor auto-sync system that fetches REAL follower counts, engagement rates, and posting frequency from social platforms. Before this task, competitors were created at `POST /api/competitors` with `followers: 0, engagementRate: 0, growthRate: 0, postingFreq: 0` and a single zero-valued snapshot — and those values were NEVER updated, so the competitor tracker view always showed flat zeros forever. This task adds a `POST /api/competitors/sync` endpoint that pulls real metrics from each platform's API and writes both an updated Competitor row and a fresh CompetitorSnapshot row.

### Files delivered (1 new)

1. **`/home/z/my-project/src/app/api/competitors/sync/route.ts`** — Authenticated POST endpoint. Body: `{ competitorId?: string }`. If `competitorId` is supplied, syncs only that competitor; otherwise syncs all competitors with `status="tracking"`. For each competitor it (1) resolves a connected `PlatformCredential` for the platform (prefers the authenticated user's credentials, then falls back to any connected credential), (2) calls the platform's real metrics API, (3) updates the Competitor row's `followers`, `engagementRate`, `postingFreq` with real values, and (4) creates a `CompetitorSnapshot` row with `date=now`, the same followers/engagement/posts values. Returns the exact response shape the task spec required:

   ```json
   {
     "ok": true,
     "synced": [{ "name": "...", "platform": "...", "followers": 12345, "snapshots": 1 }],
     "errors": ["Competitor X: no API credentials for platform Y"],
     "total": 5, "updated": 3
   }
   ```

### Platform-specific fetchers (all in the same file)

- **Twitter/X** — `fetchTwitterStats()`. Uses `oauth2UserToken` → `accessToken` → `bearerToken` (in that priority order) for `Authorization: Bearer {token}`. Calls `GET https://api.twitter.com/2/users/by/username/{handle}?user.fields=public_metrics` → `data.public_metrics.{followers_count, tweet_count}`. Then calls `GET /2/users/{userId}/tweets?max_results=20&tweet.fields=public_metrics,created_at&exclude=retweets` to compute engagement rate as `((avg of like_count + reply_count + retweet_count + quote_count) / followers) * 100` and posting frequency as the count of tweets in the last 7 days. Engagement fetch failures are non-fatal — the followers + tweet_count are still returned.
- **Instagram** — `fetchInstagramStats()`. Uses `cred.accessToken` + `cred.pageId` (the IG Business Account ID). Calls `GET https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/{ig_business_id}?fields=followers_count,media_count&access_token={token}` for the profile metrics, then `GET /v19.0/{ig_business_id}/media?fields=id,like_count,comments_count,timestamp&limit=20` for engagement (avg `like_count + comments_count` per media divided by followers) and posting frequency (media count in last 7 days).
- **Facebook** — `fetchFacebookStats()`. Uses `cred.accessToken` + `cred.pageId` (the FB Page ID). Calls `GET https://graph.facebook.com/v19.0/{page_id}?fields=fan_count,posts.limit(20){created_time,likes.limit(1).summary(true),comments.limit(1).summary(true)}&access_token={token}`. Engagement rate = avg `likes.summary.total_count + comments.summary.total_count` per post / `fan_count` * 100. Posting frequency = posts in last 7 days.
- **LinkedIn** — `fetchLinkedInStats()`. Uses `cred.accessToken` + `cred.profileId` (LinkedIn URN). Calls `GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/organizations/{orgId}?fields=followerCount` with `Authorization: Bearer {token}` + `X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0`. LinkedIn v2 only exposes the follower count via this endpoint — post counts/engagement would require the Marketing API + an organization URN, so those are returned as zero for now (acknowledged as "limited" in the task spec).

### Helper functions

- `normalizePlatform(p)` — lowercases + maps `"x"` → `"twitter"` so both Account.platform values and Competitor.platform values match the PlatformCredential.platform values (which the schema documents as `"twitter"`).
- `cleanHandle(h)` — strips leading `@` and trims whitespace (competitor handles are stored as `"@competitor1"`).
- `hasUsableToken(cred)` — returns true if any of `accessToken`, `bearerToken`, `oauth2UserToken` is set, so we don't even attempt the API call when there's no usable token.
- `computeEngagementRate(totalEng, postCount, followers)` — `(avg engagement / followers) * 100`, clamped to >= 0, guarded against `postCount <= 0 || followers <= 0`.
- `countRecent(items)` — counts items with `timestamp` ISO strings within the last 7 days for the posting-frequency metric.

### Data flow

```
POST /api/competitors/sync
  │
  ├─ requireAuth(req) → 401 if no JWT
  ├─ body: { competitorId? }
  │
  ├─ db.competitor.findMany({ where: competitorId ? {id} : {status:"tracking"} })
  │
  └─ for each competitor:
       ├─ normalizePlatform + cleanHandle
       ├─ find PlatformCredential (userId-scoped first, then any connected)
       │    └─ none? → push error "no API credentials for platform X" and continue
       ├─ fetchPlatformStats() → platform-specific fetcher
       │    └─ returns null on failure → push error "failed to fetch data from X"
       ├─ db.competitor.update({ followers, engagementRate, postingFreq })
       ├─ db.competitorSnapshot.create({ date: now, followers, engagement, posts })
       └─ push { name, platform, followers, snapshots: 1 } to synced[]
  │
  └─ return { ok: true, synced, errors, total, updated }
```

### Design choices

- **`requireAuth` (not `requireRole`).** The task spec said "auth required (use `requireAuth`)" so the endpoint uses `requireAuth` — any authenticated user (member+ can read) can trigger a sync. This matches the existing `POST /api/sync/comments` route, which also uses `requireAuth`. If we later want to restrict bulk syncs to managers/admins, that's a one-line swap to `requireRole(req, "manager")`.
- **Per-competitor try/catch.** Each competitor's sync is wrapped in its own try/catch so a single API failure (rate limit, network, 4xx) doesn't abort the whole batch — the failure is pushed to `errors[]` and the loop continues. This matches the `comments` route's per-account pattern.
- **Credential resolution: user-scoped first, then any.** The PlatformCredential model is per-user. The sync prefers the authenticated user's credentials (`userId: user.userId`), then falls back to ANY connected credential for that platform. This way: (a) if the user has connected their own Twitter/FB/IG, their credentials are used; (b) if not, but another team member connected the platform, those credentials are used; (c) if no one in the tenant has connected the platform, the competitor is skipped with an error message. This is the most useful behavior for a multi-user team workspace.
- **Token priority for Twitter.** `oauth2UserToken` (OAuth 2.0 user-context, from "Login with X") is preferred over `accessToken` (OAuth 1.0a) over `bearerToken` (app-only), because the user-context token has the broadest read scope and is what the existing `sync/twitter` route uses. App-only Bearer tokens can read public user data but cannot fetch a user's recent tweets without elevated permissions, so it's the last resort.
- **Engagement rate is computed, not directly returned.** None of the platform APIs return an "engagement rate" field — they return raw like/comment/retweet counts. We compute it as `(avg engagements per post / followers) * 100` to match the same definition used elsewhere in the app (e.g. the analytics dashboard's "Engagement Rate" KPI). This is a percentage in the range 0–100, stored directly in `engagementRate`.
- **Posting frequency = posts in last 7 days.** The schema documents `postingFreq` as "posts/week", and the most accurate way to compute that from a single API call is to count the recent items (tweets/media/posts) whose timestamp falls within the last 7 days. This is approximate (Twitter's `max_results=20` may not include a full week if the competitor posts >20 times/week), but it's a real number derived from real data, not zero.
- **Snapshots are always created, never updated.** Each sync creates a new `CompetitorSnapshot` row with `date=now` — the existing `GET /api/competitors` route already orders snapshots by `date asc` and exposes them as a `series` array for the chart. Adding a new row per sync is exactly what builds the historical trendline.
- **No schema changes.** The Competitor model already had `followers`, `engagementRate`, `growthRate`, `postingFreq` fields — we only update three of them (growthRate is intentionally NOT touched here because it requires comparing today's follower count against a previous snapshot, which is a separate calculation that could be a follow-up task). CompetitorSnapshot already had `followers`, `engagement`, `posts` — all three are populated.
- **No silent skips.** When we can't sync a competitor (no credential, API failure), the reason is pushed to `errors[]` so the client UI can show "Competitor X: no API credentials for platform Y" instead of the sync just silently doing nothing. The `errors` array is part of the documented response shape.

### Verification

- **`npx eslint "src/app/api/competitors/sync/route.ts"`** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`bun run lint`** → 1 error total, but in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` (pre-existing, unrelated — see tasks `1-synque-logo`, `2-print-formats-unique`, `1b-linkbio-public` for prior context). The new file contributes 0 errors.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** → 53 errors total, ALL pre-existing and in unrelated files (`examples/websocket/*`, `mini-services/scheduler-service/*`, `mini-services/whatsapp-service/*`, `prisma.config.ts`, `skills/image-edit/*`, `skills/stock-analysis-skill/*`, `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts`, `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts`). **Zero TypeScript errors in `src/app/api/competitors/sync/route.ts`** — confirmed by `grep -E "competitors" /tmp/tsc_out.txt` returning no matches.

### Notes / non-goals

- **No cron / scheduler.** This task adds the endpoint; calling it on a schedule (e.g. daily via the existing scheduler-service or a Vercel cron) is a separate concern. The endpoint is designed to be safe to call repeatedly — each call creates a new snapshot row, which is the intended behavior for a trendline.
- **No growthRate computation.** The `growthRate` field on Competitor is intentionally left untouched. Computing it requires comparing the new follower count against the previous snapshot's follower count — a forward-looking enhancement, not in scope for this task.
- **No UI changes.** The competitor tracker view (`src/components/views/competitors.tsx` or similar) presumably already has a "Sync" button or auto-polling — wiring that up to call `POST /api/competitors/sync` is a frontend task, not in scope here. The endpoint is ready to call as-is.
- **No de-duplication of snapshots per day.** If `POST /api/competitors/sync` is called twice in the same day, two snapshot rows will be created for that day. This matches the existing seed pattern (the original `POST /api/competitors` creates one snapshot on creation) and is what the `series` array expects — one data point per sync, not one per day.
- **LinkedIn post count + engagement is intentionally zero.** LinkedIn v2's `/organizations/{id}` endpoint only returns `followerCount` for organizations. Post counts and engagement require the Marketing API (`/v2/socialActions` / `/v2/ugcPosts`) plus an organization URN that the user has admin rights to — out of scope here, marked as "limited" in the task spec. The followerCount IS real, so LinkedIn competitors will at least show real follower counts.
- **No retry / backoff.** The endpoint makes at most 2 API calls per competitor (1 for profile, 1 for recent posts/media). If either hits a rate limit (Twitter returns 429, Facebook returns 4 or 17 sub-codes), the catch-block pushes the error and moves on — no exponential backoff. For a small competitor list (typical: 5–20), this is fine; for a large list (100+), a queue with backoff would be needed and is out of scope.
