## Task ID: 1d — `1d-mention-ingestion`

**Task**: Build a mention ingestion system that actually searches social platforms for mentions matching the user's saved `ListeningQuery` records. The `Mention` table was always empty because nothing populated it. This task adds a real sync endpoint that fetches mentions from X/Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, and Google News, classifies sentiment via the existing LLM service, deduplicates by URL, and inserts the survivors into `Mention`.

### Files delivered
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/app/api/listening/sync/route.ts` — `POST /api/listening/sync` (auth required)

### What was built

**`POST /api/listening/sync`**
- Auth required via `requireAuth(req)` — 401 if no JWT.
- Body: `{ queryId?: string }`
  - If `queryId` provided → sync only that single listening query.
  - If omitted → sync ALL queries with `status: "active"`.
- For each query, parses `keywords` (comma-separated), then searches FOUR sources per query:
  1. **X / Twitter** — `GET https://api.twitter.com/2/tweets/search/recent?query=…&max_results=30` with `tweet.fields=created_at,public_metrics,author_id` and `expansions=author_id` + `user.fields=name,username,profile_image_url`. Requires a connected `PlatformCredential` for platform `twitter` or `x` (any team member's). Token priority: `oauth2UserToken` → `accessToken` (OAuth 1.0a) → `bearerToken` (app-only). Returns 30 tweets per query. Each tweet becomes a mention with `source="x"`, author = `@username`, `reach = impression_count`, `engagement = likes+replies+retweets+quotes`, `url = twitter.com/i/web/status/{id}`.
  2. **Instagram** — two-step IG Graph API call: `GET /v19.0/ig_hashtag_search?user_id={ig_business_id}&q={keyword}` → resolves hashtag ID, then `GET /v19.0/{hashtag_id}/recent_media?user_id={ig_business_id}&fields=id,caption,permalink,like_count,comments_count,timestamp,username`. Requires IG Business account (`PlatformCredential` with `accessToken` + `pageId` = IG Business Account ID). Limited to first keyword only (IG hashtag search is single-tag). Each media item becomes a mention with `source="instagram"`, `engagement = likes+comments`.
  3. **Facebook** — SKIPPED (Graph API does not support keyword search). Logged once to `errors[]`.
  4. **Reddit** — `GET https://www.reddit.com/search.json?q={query}&sort=new&limit=25`. Public endpoint, no auth needed. A descriptive User-Agent (`SYNQUE-listening/1.0`) is set per Reddit's API policy. Each result becomes a mention with `source="reddit"`, author = `u/{username}`, `reach = score`, `engagement = num_comments`, `url = https://www.reddit.com{permalink}`.
  5. **Google News** — `GET https://news.google.com/rss/search?q={query}&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US:en`. Returns RSS XML — no auth needed. Parsed with a regex-based RSS parser (no XML library dependency). Each `<item>` becomes a mention with `source="news"`, author = the `<source>` tag's text (the publisher), text = title + description (HTML stripped, entities decoded), `url = <link>` content.

**Deduplication**: Before insertion, all candidate mentions have their URLs collected into a Set. A single `db.mention.findMany({ where: { url: { in: [...] } }, select: { url: true } })` query checks which URLs already exist in the DB. Any candidate whose URL is in that set (or whose URL is null AND a duplicate of a null-URL candidate — though in practice this only filters null URLs by the second null pass, which we deliberately allow because null-URL mentions have no URL to dedup by) is filtered out.

Wait — actually re-read the dedup logic: candidates with `url: null` are NOT filtered out (the filter is `!r.raw.url || !existingUrls.has(r.raw.url)`). That means null-URL mentions always pass through. This is intentional: Reddit and Google News almost always return a URL, and Twitter always returns one (`twitter.com/i/web/status/{id}`), so in practice null URLs are rare and represent mentions we can't dedup against anyway. We'd rather store them than silently drop them.

**Sentiment classification**: All surviving candidates are batched into a single `classifySentimentBatch()` call (LLM with keyword fallback — never returns "unknown"). The batch function classifies ≤5 items individually, >5 items in a single LLM call with numbered lines. Each mention's classified sentiment (`positive` | `neutral` | `negative`) is stored in the `Mention.sentiment` column.

**Insertion**: Each mention is inserted with a per-row try/catch so a single DB failure (e.g. constraint violation on a race) doesn't abort the whole batch — the failure is pushed to `errors[]` and the loop continues.

**Response shape** (exactly matches the task spec):
```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "totalQueries": <number of ListeningQuery records processed>,
  "totalFound": <raw mentions discovered across all platforms, before dedup>,
  "newMentions": <number actually inserted into Mention table>,
  "classified": <number for which sentiment was classified = newCandidates.length>,
  "errors": [<per-query, per-platform, or one-time error strings>]
}
```

### Data flow

```
POST /api/listening/sync
  │
  ├─ requireAuth(req) → 401 if no JWT
  ├─ body: { queryId? }
  │
  ├─ db.listeningQuery.findMany({ where: queryId ? {id} : {status:"active"} })
  │     → if 0 queries, early return { ok, totalQueries:0, … }
  │
  ├─ db.platformCredential.findFirst({ twitter|x, connected:true })  ← pre-fetch once
  ├─ db.platformCredential.findFirst({ instagram, connected:true })   ← pre-fetch once
  │
  └─ for each query q:
       ├─ parse keywords (split "," + trim + filter empties)
       │    └─ if none → push error "Query X: no keywords defined" + continue
       │
       ├─ [Twitter] if cred:  searchTwitter(q.keywords JOIN " OR ", cred)
       │     └─ catch → push error "Query X [twitter]: …"
       ├─ [Instagram] if cred.accessToken + cred.pageId:  searchInstagramHashtag(firstKeyword, cred)
       │     └─ catch → push error "Query X [instagram]: …"
       ├─ [Facebook] skipped (note logged once after loop)
       ├─ [Reddit]  searchReddit(q.keywords JOIN " ")
       │     └─ catch → push error "Query X [reddit]: …"
       └─ [News]    searchGoogleNews(q.keywords JOIN " ")
             └─ catch → push error "Query X [news]: …"
  │
  ├─ errors.push("Facebook: skipped — Graph API does not support keyword search")
  ├─ if !twitterCred: errors.push("Twitter: skipped — no connected PlatformCredential…")
  ├─ if !igCred || !accessToken || !pageId: errors.push("Instagram: skipped — …")
  │
  ├─ collect allRaw[].url → deduped Set<string>
  ├─ db.mention.findMany({ where: { url: { in: [...] } }, select: { url: true } })
  │     → existingUrls Set
  │
  ├─ newCandidates = allRaw.filter(url is null OR url not in existingUrls)
  │
  ├─ classifySentimentBatch(newCandidates.map(text))  ← single LLM call (or keyword fallback)
  │
  ├─ for each newCandidate: db.mention.create({ … })  ← per-row try/catch
  │     └─ catch → push error "Insert failed for {url|author}: …"
  │
  └─ return { ok:true, totalQueries, totalFound, newMentions, classified, errors }
```

### Design choices

- **`requireAuth` (not `requireRole`).** Task spec explicitly said "Auth required (use `requireAuth`)". Any authenticated user can trigger a mention sync. Same pattern as the existing `POST /api/sync/comments` and `POST /api/competitors/sync` routes.
- **Per-platform try/catch inside per-query try block.** Each `(query, platform)` pair is independently wrapped — a Twitter rate-limit, Instagram 403, Reddit 5xx, or News RSS hiccup pushes an entry to `errors[]` and the loop continues to the next platform. A single platform failure never aborts the whole sync.
- **Credentials resolved ONCE, not per query.** `db.platformCredential.findFirst` is called once before the loop. The same Twitter/IG credential is reused across all queries (otherwise we'd issue N+ identical DB queries). This matches the `competitors/sync` route's pattern.
- **First available credential (any team member's).** `findFirst` with `connected: true` — does NOT filter by the authenticated user's `userId`. This means if any team member has connected their Twitter account in Settings → Platform API Keys, that token is used. Same shared-credential philosophy as `competitors/sync`.
- **Twitter token priority: oauth2UserToken → accessToken → bearerToken.** The OAuth 2.0 user-context token (from "Login with X") has the broadest read scope, including the recent search endpoint. The OAuth 1.0a access token is the next best. The app-only Bearer Token is the last resort (it can also call `tweets/search/recent` for public tweets, but with lower rate limits). All three work with this endpoint per Twitter API v2 docs.
- **Keyword handling**: the `ListeningQuery.keywords` field is documented as "comma separated". We split on commas, trim, filter empties, then:
  - **Twitter**: join with `" OR "` so each comma-separated keyword becomes an alternative match. Twitter's search syntax treats spaces as AND by default, so `"acme OR #brand"` matches tweets containing either "acme" or "#brand". Multi-word keywords within one comma-separated entry stay together (e.g. `"Acme Corp"` → matches tweets containing both "Acme" AND "Corp").
  - **Reddit + Google News**: join with `" "` (space) since their search APIs treat spaces as natural separators. Reddit's `q` parameter is a simple full-text search; Google News RSS `q` accepts space-separated keywords.
- **Instagram limited to first keyword only.** The IG hashtag search API (`ig_hashtag_search`) accepts a single `q` value (one hashtag, no spaces, no OR). So we strip leading `#` from `keywordsList[0]`, take the first whitespace-separated token, and search for just that one tag. The other keywords are silently ignored for IG. If a query has `keywords: "acme, #brand"`, IG searches only for "acme".
- **Mention text truncated to 500 chars.** Tweet text, IG captions, Reddit `selftext`, and News descriptions are all `.slice(0, 500)` before storage. This keeps the DB rows small and the LLM sentiment classification fast (sentiment is usually determinable from the first sentence).
- **Mention `source` values**: `"x"` for Twitter (matches schema comment `// instagram | x | facebook | web | reddit | news`), `"instagram"` for IG, `"reddit"` for Reddit, `"news"` for Google News. The existing `POST /api/listening/[id]/reply` route handles both `"x"` and `"twitter"` for Twitter reply routing.
- **No XML library dependency.** Google News RSS is parsed with a regex-based `parseRssItems()` function — `<item>…</item>` blocks are extracted, then individual tags (`<title>`, `<link>`, `<pubDate>`, `<source>`, `<description>`) are extracted with a CDATA-aware regex. The `package.json` doesn't include `fast-xml-parser` or `xml2js`, so this avoids a new dependency. Decoding of the 5 core XML entities (`&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot; &apos;`) is handled by `decodeEntities()`. HTML in the `<description>` is stripped by `stripHtml()`.
- **Batch sentiment classification.** `classifySentimentBatch()` from `@/lib/sentiment` is called once with all new candidates. For batches >5 it issues a single LLM call with a numbered list ("1. text\n2. text\n…"); for ≤5 it classifies individually. Either way it ALWAYS returns a sentiment per item (LLM with keyword fallback). This means `classified = newCandidates.length` (every candidate gets classified, even if classification falls back to keyword matching).
- **`classified` ≠ `newMentions`**. The two are different on purpose: `classified` counts how many mentions had their sentiment determined (= `newCandidates.length`, since the batch always returns a result for every input). `newMentions` counts how many actually got inserted (= `inserted` counter, which can be lower if individual `db.mention.create` calls fail). This lets the UI distinguish "found N new mentions and tried to classify them all" from "successfully inserted M of N".
- **Facebook skipped, not silent.** The Graph API does not support keyword search (only page-scoped post search with `page_access_token`). We log a single one-time note to `errors[]` explaining the skip — never per-query, to avoid spamming the array. Same treatment for missing Twitter/IG credentials: one note each, after the loop.
- **`maxDuration = 60`.** Multi-platform sync with N queries × 4 platforms × network calls can easily exceed the default 10s serverless function limit. 60s is the same value used by `competitors/sync`.
- **No schema changes.** The `Mention` model already had every field we need (`queryId, source, author, authorAvatar, text, url, sentiment, reach, engagement, date`). The `ListeningQuery` model already had `keywords` (comma-separated). The `PlatformCredential` model already had `accessToken`, `bearerToken`, `oauth2UserToken`, `pageId`. We only INSERT new Mention rows — never UPDATE existing ones.
- **No UI changes.** The listening view (`src/components/views/listening.tsx` or similar) presumably already has a "Sync" button or polling interval — wiring that up to call `POST /api/listening/sync` is a frontend task, not in scope here. The endpoint is ready to call as-is.

### Verification

- **`npx eslint src/app/api/listening/sync/route.ts`** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`bun run lint`** → 1 error total, but in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js` (pre-existing, unrelated — same as documented in tasks `1-synque-logo`, `2-print-formats-unique`, `1b-linkbio-public`, `1c-competitors-sync`). The new file contributes 0 errors.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** → 53 errors total, ALL pre-existing in unrelated files (`examples/websocket/*`, `mini-services/scheduler-service/*`, `mini-services/whatsapp-service/*`, `prisma.config.ts`, `skills/image-edit/*`, `skills/stock-analysis-skill/*`, `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts`, `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts`). **Zero TypeScript errors in `src/app/api/listening/sync/route.ts`** — verified by `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep "listening/sync"` returning no matches. (Initial run flagged one type incompatibility on `Set<string | null>` vs `Set<string>` because `Mention.url` is nullable — fixed by filtering out nulls with `(u): u is string => Boolean(u)` before constructing the Set.)

### Notes / non-goals

- **No cron / scheduler.** This task adds the endpoint only. Calling it on a schedule (e.g. daily via the existing `scheduler-service`, Vercel cron, or a UI "Sync" button) is a separate concern. The endpoint is safe to call repeatedly — duplicates are deduplicated by URL, so a second sync won't double-insert.
- **No pagination / infinite scroll.** Each platform returns a fixed cap per query: Twitter 30, IG 25, Reddit 25, News ~100 (Google News RSS doesn't paginate). For a typical 5-query listening dashboard, that's ~540 max mentions per sync — well within the 60s `maxDuration`. If a customer needs more, they should narrow their keywords or split into more granular queries.
- **No keyword negation / advanced query syntax.** The user can manually include Twitter search operators in their `keywords` field (e.g. `"acme -spam"`, `"#acme since:2024-01-01"`) and Twitter will interpret them. Reddit + Google News ignore most operators. We don't validate or transform the query — we pass it through (after comma-splitting + OR-joining for Twitter).
- **Instagram hashtag search needs IG Business approval.** The `ig_hashtag_search` endpoint requires App Review for the `instagram_manage_insights` permission (and the IG account must be a Business account, not Creator). If the user hasn't completed App Review, the API returns 403 / 10 sub-code, and we log the error and move on. Mention ingestion still works for Twitter + Reddit + News without IG.
- **Twitter recent search only goes back 7 days.** The `tweets/search/recent` endpoint only returns tweets from the last 7 days. Historical search requires the academic / enterprise `tweets/search/all` endpoint (and a separate tier of API access). For ongoing listening, 7 days is fine — run the sync daily.
- **Reddit `score` is not "reach".** Reddit's `score` is the upvote-minus-downvote net — it's a quality signal, not a view count. We store it as `reach` because the schema doesn't have a `score` field. Reddit doesn't expose view counts via the public API (only via the authenticated `r/{sub}/about/{post}/` endpoint). This is a reasonable approximation: high-score posts are more "visible" in the sense of reaching the front page.
- **Google News `reach`/`engagement` are 0.** RSS doesn't expose view counts or social engagement metrics. We store 0 for both. The news mention's value is in the existence + sentiment + URL, not in impression numbers.
- **No retry / backoff.** Each platform gets one fetch attempt per query. Twitter's recent search has a 450-req-per-15-min app-only rate limit (75 with user-context) — for 5–20 queries, well within limits. If a customer has 100+ queries, they should consider staggering the sync or splitting into batches. Out of scope here.
- **No team-scoping of mentions.** Mentions are created against the global `ListeningQuery` table (not filtered by `customerId`). The existing `GET /api/listening` route also returns all mentions globally. Multi-tenant isolation of listening queries is a separate concern (the `ListeningQuery` model doesn't currently have a `customerId` field).

## Task ID: 2 — `2-security-features`

**Task**: Implement the four missing security features end-to-end: (a) TOTP-based 2FA with login flow, (b) DB-backed session tracking with list/revoke/logout, (c) DB-backed password reset replacing the in-memory `color`-field hack, (d) DB-backed email verification replacing the in-memory `title`-field hack. The Prisma schema already had `User.emailVerified`, `User.totpSecret`, `User.twoFactorEnabled`, `User.sessions`, and the new `Session`, `PasswordResetToken`, `EmailVerificationToken` models — the task was to build the API surface that uses them.

### Files delivered

**New shared libraries (4)**
1. `src/lib/totp.ts` — RFC 6238 / RFC 4648 implementation using only `node:crypto` (no `otplib` dependency). Exports `generateTotpSecret()`, `verifyTotp(token, secret, now?)`, `buildOtpAuthUri({ secret, email, issuer })`, plus `base32Encode`/`base32Decode` helpers. `verifyTotp` accepts ±1 window (±30s) for clock skew and uses constant-time comparison to defend against timing attacks.
2. `src/lib/2fa-temp-token.ts` — short-lived (5-min) JWT used as the bridge between `/api/auth/login` (password verified, but 2FA pending) and `/api/auth/2fa/login` (TOTP verified, full session issued). The token has `type: "2fa-pending"` and `verify2faTempToken` rejects any token that isn't of this type — so a regular session JWT can't be reused as a temp token.
3. `src/lib/auth-session.ts` — shared `issueSession({ user, req })` helper that signs the JWT, captures `userAgent` + `ipAddress` from request headers, creates the `Session` row, and returns `{ token, sessionExpiresAt, userPublic }`. Also exports `setAuthCookie`, `revokeSessionByToken`, `buildUserPublic`. Used by `/login`, `/2fa/login`, `/signup`, `/demo` so session creation logic lives in one place.
4. `src/lib/email.ts` — `sendEmail({ to, subject, text })` wraps the `MailServer` row + nodemailer transport (extracted from the inline duplication in `forgot-password` + `verify-email`). `buildAppUrl(req, path)` resolves `proto://host/path` from `x-forwarded-host` / `x-forwarded-proto` headers (Vercel proxy aware). `sendVerificationEmail({ req, email, name })` creates an `EmailVerificationToken` row (invalidating prior unused ones for the same email first) + sends the email — used by both `/signup` (auto-send) and `/verify-email` (user-initiated resend).

**New API routes (10)**
5. `src/app/api/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts` (POST) — generates a 32-char base32 secret, stores it on `user.totpSecret`, sets `twoFactorEnabled = false` (must verify before enabling), returns `{ secret, otpauth, previouslyEnabled }`. The `otpauth` URI is `otpauth://totp/SYNQUE:email?secret=...&issuer=SYNQUE&algorithm=SHA1&digits=6&period=30` — drop-in for any QR code generator.
6. `src/app/api/auth/2fa/verify/route.ts` (POST) — verifies a 6-digit code against the stored secret, enables 2FA on success. Rejects with a clear message if no secret has been set up yet.
7. `src/app/api/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts` (POST) — clears `totpSecret` + sets `twoFactorEnabled = false`. If a `code` is supplied in the body, verifies it first (defends against a hijacked session disabling 2FA without the user's authenticator). Idempotent on already-disabled state.
8. `src/app/api/auth/2fa/login/route.ts` (POST) — accepts `{ tempToken, code }`, verifies the temp token (5-min TTL, type-checked), looks up the user, rejects suspended accounts, verifies the TOTP code, then calls `issueSession` to issue the full session JWT + create the Session row.
9. `src/app/api/auth/sessions/route.ts` (GET) — lists active (non-revoked, non-expired) sessions for the current user, newest first, with `current: true` on the one matching the request's token. Parses a friendly `{ device, browser, os }` from the User-Agent string (no external UA library).
10. `src/app/api/auth/sessions/[id]/route.ts` (DELETE) — revokes a single session by setting `revokedAt = now()`. Scoped to `userId` (a user can't revoke another user's session by guessing ids). Returns `revokedCurrent: true` if the revoked session was the request's own — the UI uses this to log the user out.
11. `src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts` (POST + GET) — revokes the current session by token + clears the auth cookie. Idempotent (safe to call with no/invalid token). GET variant is a redirect-style logout for the cookie-based flow.
12. `src/app/api/auth/verify-reset-token/route.ts` (GET) — checks if a reset token is valid (exists, not expired, not used). Returns `{ valid: true, email }` for good tokens, `{ valid: false, reason: "expired" | "used" }` for bad-but-known ones, 400 for unknown tokens. Used by the "enter new password" page to decide whether to show the form before the user types.
13. `src/app/api/auth/verify-email/confirm/route.ts` (GET) — the email-link callback. Verifies the token, sets `user.emailVerified = now()`, marks the token as used (single transaction). Idempotent on already-verified state (returns `alreadyVerified: true`). Does NOT log the user in — they must authenticate separately so a stolen link can't be combined with an existing session.
14. `src/app/api/auth/verify-email/route.ts` (POST, rewritten) — was previously a stub that stored the token in the user's `title` field as `verify:xxx`. Now uses `EmailVerificationToken` + `sendVerificationEmail`. Accepts the email from the authenticated user's record (preferred) or a body-supplied email (pre-login flow). Same response shape regardless of whether the email exists (no enumeration).

**Modified files (8)**
15. `src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts` — now selects `emailVerified`, `totpSecret`, `twoFactorEnabled`, `status` from the DB. After password verification, if `user.twoFactorEnabled && user.totpSecret`, returns `{ requires2FA: true, tempToken, email }` instead of issuing a session. Otherwise calls `issueSession({ user, req })` to create the JWT + Session row + cookie in one place. Also rejects suspended accounts (was previously allowed in).
16. `src/app/api/auth/signup/route.ts` — normalizes email to lowercase, uses `issueSession` (so a Session row is created on signup too), auto-sends a verification email after user creation (best-effort — never fails signup if the mail server is down), surfaces `emailVerificationSent` + `verifyUrl` (the latter only when no mail server is configured, for dev/test) in the response, and includes `emailVerified` + `twoFactorEnabled` in the user object.
17. `src/app/api/auth/demo/route.ts` — refactored to use `issueSession` (so the demo user gets a Session row too — previously demo sessions were invisible to `/sessions`). Split the DB lookup into a `findDemoUser()` helper so `let user` could be explicitly typed (TS was narrowing `let user = null` to `null`). Returns `emailVerified` + `twoFactorEnabled` in the user object.
18. `src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts` — added `emailVerified` + `twoFactorEnabled` to the Prisma `select` so the `/api/auth/me` response (consumed by `fetchUser`) carries them.
19. `src/app/api/auth/forgot-password/route.ts` — was storing the token in the user's `color` field as `reset:token:expires`. Now inserts a row into `PasswordResetToken` with a 1-hour `expiresAt`, invalidates prior unused tokens for the same email first (so only the newest link is valid), uses the shared `sendEmail` helper. Same response shape (no enumeration).
20. `src/app/api/auth/reset-password/route.ts` — was scanning `User.color` for `startsWith("reset:token:")`. Now looks up the token in `PasswordResetToken`, checks `usedAt` + `expiresAt`, hashes the new password + marks the token as used in a `db.$transaction`. Also revokes all of the user's active sessions on password reset (so an attacker who already had a session can't keep using it after the user resets).
21. `src/lib/auth-guard.ts` — added `getRawToken(req)` (extracts the JWT from Bearer header or cookie) and `requireAuthWithSession(req)` — an async variant of `requireAuth` that also looks up the `Session` row and rejects (401) if the session is revoked or expired. Falls back gracefully to JWT-only check if the DB lookup fails (don't lock users out during Neon cold-starts). Ordinary read routes keep using the sync `requireAuth` to avoid the extra round-trip.
22. `src/lib/auth-store.ts` — `AuthUser` interface gained `emailVerified?: string | null` + `twoFactorEnabled?: boolean`. Added `pending2FA: { tempToken; email } | null` state + `complete2faLogin(code)` action so the client can drive the 2FA login flow. `login()` now detects `{ requires2FA: true }` from the server and stashes the temp token instead of completing login. `logout()` is now async and calls `POST /api/auth/logout` to revoke the server-side session before clearing local state.

### Endpoints + behavior summary

| Method | Route | Body / Query | Returns | Notes |
|--------|-------|--------------|---------|-------|
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | `{ email, password }` | `{ token, user }` OR `{ requires2FA: true, tempToken, email }` | 2FA-aware |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa/login` | `{ tempToken, code }` | `{ token, user }` | completes 2FA login |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa/setup` | (auth) | `{ secret, otpauth, previouslyEnabled }` | generates new TOTP secret |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa/verify` | `{ code }` (auth) | `{ ok, twoFactorEnabled }` | enables 2FA |
| POST | `/api/auth/2fa/disable` | `{ code? }` (auth) | `{ ok, twoFactorEnabled: false }` | disables 2FA |
| POST | `/api/auth/signup` | `{ name, email, password, company? }` | `{ token, user, emailVerificationSent, verifyUrl? }` | auto-sends verify email |
| POST | `/api/auth/demo` | — | `{ token, user, demo: true }` | demo viewer login |
| GET  | `/api/auth/me` | (auth) | `{ user }` | now includes `emailVerified` + `twoFactorEnabled` |
| POST | `/api/auth/logout` | (auth optional) | `{ ok: true }` | revokes session + clears cookie |
| GET  | `/api/auth/sessions` | (auth) | `{ sessions: [...] }` | list active sessions |
| DELETE | `/api/auth/sessions/[id]` | (auth) | `{ ok, revokedCurrent }` | revoke a session |
| POST | `/api/auth/forgot-password` | `{ email }` | `{ ok, message, sent?, resetUrl? }` | DB-backed token |
| GET  | `/api/auth/verify-reset-token?token=` | — | `{ valid, email? }` or `{ valid: false, reason }` | for the reset-password page |
| POST | `/api/auth/reset-password` | `{ token, newPassword }` | `{ ok, message }` | DB-backed + revokes sessions |
| POST | `/api/auth/verify-email` | `{ email? }` (auth optional) | `{ ok, message, sent?, verifyUrl? }` | DB-backed token |
| GET  | `/api/auth/verify-email/confirm?token=` | — | `{ ok, message, alreadyVerified? }` | the email-link callback |

### Security decisions

- **TOTP without external dependency.** `otplib` is not installed and adding a runtime dep just for one algorithm is wasteful. `src/lib/totp.ts` is a ~80-line RFC 6238 implementation using only `node:crypto` (HMAC-SHA1 + dynamic truncation). `verifyTotp` accepts the current ±1 30-second windows (so a user whose phone clock drifts slightly still succeeds) and uses constant-time comparison so an attacker can't timing-attack the comparison.
- **2FA login flow uses a typed temp token.** The login route verifies the password, then if 2FA is enabled it returns a 5-minute JWT with `type: "2fa-pending"` and `userId`. `verify2faTempToken` rejects any token without that type — so a regular session JWT can't be substituted. This avoids persisting a "pending login" row in the DB and avoids the alternative of stashing the password in a cookie.
- **Session table is the source of truth for revocation.** Every successful login (regular, 2FA, demo, signup) creates a `Session` row via `issueSession`. Logout + password reset + session revoke all set `revokedAt`. `requireAuthWithSession` is provided for sensitive routes (account deletion, billing) where revocation must take effect immediately; ordinary read routes keep the synchronous `requireAuth` to avoid the extra round-trip — the JWT signature check is sufficient for them. The auth-guard falls back to JWT-only if the session lookup DB query fails (don't lock users out during Neon cold-starts).
- **Password reset revokes all active sessions for the user.** When a user successfully resets their password, `db.session.updateMany` sets `revokedAt` on every active session they had. This means an attacker who already had a valid session token can't keep using it after the victim resets — they're forced to re-authenticate with the new password.
- **Password reset does NOT auto-login the user.** The endpoint returns `{ ok: true }` and tells the user to log in with their new password. This means a stolen reset link can't be combined with an existing session to silently take over an account — the attacker would need to also know the new password.
- **Email verification does NOT auto-login.** Same reasoning — `/verify-email/confirm` just sets `user.emailVerified` and tells the user to log in.
- **No account enumeration.** `/forgot-password` and `/verify-email` return the same response shape regardless of whether the email exists. `/verify-reset-token` returns `valid: false` with `reason: "invalid"` for unknown tokens, but `reason: "expired" | "used"` for known-but-bad ones — this is intentional because by the time the user has a token URL, they already know the email exists, so distinguishing "expired" vs "invalid" is a UX win without leaking anything.
- **2FA setup re-running clears `twoFactorEnabled`.** If a user who already had 2FA on re-runs `/2fa/setup`, we set `twoFactorEnabled = false` until they verify a code with the new secret. This prevents a stale secret (e.g. from before they lost their phone) from being usable to log in.
- **All new routes export `dynamic = "force-dynamic"`.** No caching — these endpoints are per-user / per-token.

### Verification

- **`npx eslint` on all 22 new/modified files** → exit 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **`bun run lint`** → 1 error total (the pre-existing `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` warning in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js`, unrelated). New/modified files contribute 0 errors.
- **`npx tsc --noEmit`** → 0 errors in any new/modified file. The 33 remaining errors are all in pre-existing files (`examples/websocket/*`, `mini-services/scheduler-service/*`, `mini-services/whatsapp-service/*`, `prisma.config.ts`, `skills/image-edit/*`, `skills/stock-analysis-skill/*`, `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts`). Verified by grepping `tsc` output for `src/app/api/auth/` and `src/lib/(auth|totp|email|2fa)` — no matches.
- **Smoke test (dev server, real HTTP requests)**:
  - `GET /api/auth/verify-reset-token?token=invalid` → 400 `{"valid":false,"reason":"invalid"}` ✓
  - `GET /api/auth/verify-email/confirm?token=invalid` → 400 `{"error":"Invalid or expired verification token"}` ✓
  - `GET /api/auth/sessions` (no auth) → 401 `{"error":"Authentication required"}` ✓
  - `POST /api/auth/2fa/setup` (no auth) → 401 `{"error":"Authentication required"}` ✓
  - `POST /api/auth/logout` (no auth) → 200 `{"ok":true}` (idempotent) ✓
  - `POST /api/auth/forgot-password` `{ email: "nonexistent@example.com" }` → 200 with the same non-revealing message as a known email ✓

### Notes / non-goals

- **No UI wiring.** The settings.tsx 2FA / sessions / login-history / API-keys / IP-allowlist cards currently render mock data or hard-coded text. Wiring them to the new endpoints is a frontend task — the API contract is documented above for whoever picks it up.
- **No 2FA recovery codes.** If a user loses their authenticator, they can't currently recover their account via the API. The disable endpoint accepts an optional `code` for safety, but if they can't generate one, an admin would need to clear `totpSecret` + `twoFactorEnabled` directly in the DB. A `/api/auth/2fa/recover` flow with backup codes is a separate concern.
- **No rate limiting on `/login`, `/2fa/login`, `/forgot-password`, `/verify-email`.** A determined attacker could brute-force TOTP codes (1 in 1,000,000 per attempt, ±1 window → ~1 in 333,333 effective) if there's no rate limit. The Neon DB is the bottleneck today, but adding a simple in-memory or Redis-backed rate limiter is recommended before launch.
- **No IP geolocation for sessions.** The `ipAddress` is stored but not geo-resolved. The UI currently shows the raw IP; adding a MaxMind GeoIP lookup is a separate task.
- **Sessions endpoint returns `lastActive = createdAt`.** The schema doesn't have a `lastActive` column on Session — we'd need to update it on every authenticated request, which is too expensive. The current `createdAt` is a reasonable approximation; if true last-active tracking is needed later, we can add the column + update it lazily (e.g. only every 5 minutes per session).
- **`/verify-reset-token` is intentionally GET, not POST.** The frontend navigates to `/reset-password?token=xxx` (a fresh page load) and needs to check the token before showing the form. GET makes this trivial; the token is already in the URL anyway (it was emailed as a query string), so there's no additional exposure from GET vs POST here.
- **`/verify-email/confirm` is GET because email clients don't follow POST links.** Standard practice — the link in the email is a GET.
- **`/api/auth/logout` supports both POST and GET.** POST is the preferred path (called by the auth-store on `logout()`). GET is for the rare redirect-style logout (e.g. clicking a link). Both are idempotent.

## Task ID: 4e — `4e-settings-security-ui`

**Task**: Wire the existing Settings → Security section UI to the NEW auth/2fa + auth/sessions API endpoints that were just built. Replace the mock/static 2FA toggle, the placeholder QR setup dialog, and the "no session tracking yet" empty state with real API calls.

### Files changed
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/views/settings.tsx` — only the `SecuritySection` component (line ~1868) and its setup dialog (line ~2412) were touched. No other sections of the file were modified.

### Endpoints wired
| UI element | Method + URL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2FA "Set up" / Switch on | `POST /api/auth/2fa/setup` | Returns `{ secret, otpauth, previouslyEnabled }` → dialog shows QR + manual secret |
| 2FA setup dialog "Verify & enable" | `POST /api/auth/2fa/verify { code }` | Server sets `user.twoFactorEnabled = true` → `fetchUser()` refreshes the toggle |
| 2FA "Disable" / Switch off | `POST /api/auth/2fa/disable` | Server clears `totpSecret` + disables → `fetchUser()` refreshes the toggle |
| Active sessions list | `GET /api/auth/sessions` (via `useApi`) | Each row: browser/OS label, IP, signed-in `timeAgo`, expiry date, "Current" badge, "Revoke" button |
| Session "Revoke" button | `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/[id]` | If `revokedCurrent === true`, calls `logout()` from the auth store (client is logged out); otherwise `reloadSessions()` |
| Password change form | unchanged | Still POSTs `/api/auth/login` to verify + PATCHes `/api/users` to set new password — verified still works |

### Implementation notes
- **2FA status is now derived, not local state.** `const twoFA = !!user?.twoFactorEnabled;` reads from the auth store. The `Set up`/`Disable` button, the `Switch`, and the status text all update automatically when `fetchUser()` refreshes the store after a successful verify/disable.
- **Bearer token pattern** is the same one used elsewhere in this file (`getAuthToken()` reads from `localStorage["socialflow-auth"]` → `state.token`). `useApi` already does this internally for the GET, so the sessions list needs no manual header. The POST/DELETE calls (setup, verify, disable, revoke) attach `Authorization: Bearer <token>` manually since they bypass `useApi`.
- **QR code rendering** uses the external service `https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?size=200x200&data=${encodeURIComponent(otpauth)}` (no client-side QR lib needed; `@next/next/no-img-element` is disabled in the project's eslint config). The raw secret is also shown for manual entry.
- **Verify-code input** strips non-digits, caps at 6 chars, uses `inputMode="numeric"` + `autoComplete="one-time-code"` (iOS Safari auto-fills from SMS-less authenticators), and submits on Enter.
- **Sessions list** uses `useApi<{ sessions: SessionRow[] }>("/api/auth/sessions")` — skeleton shimmer while loading, "No active sessions" empty state, Refresh button in the section header.
- **Revoke flow** asks `window.confirm` before DELETE. If the server says `revokedCurrent: true` (i.e. the user revoked their own current session), it calls `logout()` from the auth store — the store then POSTs `/api/auth/logout`, clears the token, and the app routes back to the login screen.
- **Login history** section was left as the honest empty state — there is no `GET /api/auth/login-history` endpoint yet (the task scope was 2FA + sessions + password only).
- **Password change** form was left untouched — it already called the right endpoints (`/api/auth/login` to verify + `/api/users` PATCH). Verified no changes needed.
- **API keys / IP allowlist** sections untouched (already wired / out of scope).

### Verification
- `npx eslint src/components/views/settings.tsx` → **0 errors, 0 warnings**
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep settings` → **0 errors** (the project has pre-existing TS errors in unrelated files: `mini-services/whatsapp-service`, `src/app/api/ai/assistant`, `src/app/api/platform-credentials/[platform]/sync` — none in `settings.tsx`, `auth-store.ts`, or `hooks.ts`)

### What's NOT done (out of scope / future work)
- Login history table still shows the empty state — needs a new `/api/auth/login-history` endpoint.
- 2FA disable flow does not currently ask for a code (the server supports an optional `{ code }` body for extra defense; the UI skips it for simplicity since `requireAuth` already gates the call). Could add a "confirm with code" step if we want the extra defense.
- The QR code is fetched from `api.qrserver.com` (external). If offline-only operation matters, swap in a client-side QR lib (e.g. `qrcode.react`) and pass the `otpauth` URI directly.

2. **4 light rays** — each a `border-radius: 50%` div with `filter: blur(70-90px)`, positioned in different screen corners:

   - Ray 2 (top-right, 55vh × 50vw): purple `rgba(150,55,210,0.5)` → green/teal via `hue-rotate(-120deg)`, animated by `mysticRay2 28s`.
   - Ray 3 (bottom-left, 55vh × 50vw): teal `rgba(20,200,180,0.5)` drifting to scale 1.3, animated by `mysticRay3 22s`.
   - Ray 4 (bottom-right, 45vh × 40vw): gold `rgba(245,180,60,0.42)` drifting to scale 1.4, animated by `mysticRay4 26s`.
3. **48 bioluminescent plankton particles** — `<span>` 1–3px dots with glowing `box-shadow`, rising from the bottom of the screen via `planktonRise` (translateY(-100vh) + horizontal `--drift` sway), 18–34s cycles, 7 alternating colors (teal-cyan, violet, pink, emerald, amber, sky blue, light violet). Reduced to 22 on mobile (`max-width: 768px` via `window.matchMedia`) for performance.
4. **Shimmer sweep** — `linear-gradient(115deg, transparent, rgba(140,200,255,0.12), transparent)` with `backgroundSize: 200% 200%`, animated by the existing `sfShimmerSweep 14s`, `opacity: 0.5`.
5. **Breathing tint** — solid `#04060A` overlay pulsing opacity 0.15 → 0.35 via `mysticBreathe 9s` for the rhythmic "living ocean" feel.
6. **Edge vignette** — `radial-gradient(ellipse at center, transparent 50%, rgba(0,0,0,0.55) 100%)` to darken corners/edges and keep foreground text readable.

All animations are pure CSS — no JS `requestAnimationFrame` loops — for 60fps performance.

### Keyframes added to `LANDING_KEYFRAMES` (lines 1822-1850)

```css
@keyframes mysticRay1   { 0%,100% { translate(0,0) scale(1);    opacity:.30; hue-rotate(0deg); }
                          33%     { translate(10%,-5%) scale(1.2); opacity:.50; hue-rotate(60deg); }
                          66%     { translate(-5%,8%) scale(0.9);  opacity:.20; hue-rotate(-30deg); } }
@keyframes mysticRay2   { 0%,100% { translate(0,0) scale(1.1);   opacity:.25; hue-rotate(0deg); }
                          50%     { translate(-8%,10%) scale(0.8); opacity:.45; hue-rotate(-120deg); } }
@keyframes mysticRay3   { 0%,100% { translate(0,0) scale(0.9);   opacity:.20; }
                          40%     { translate(12%,-8%) scale(1.3); opacity:.40; }
                          80%     { translate(-6%,5%) scale(1);   opacity:.30; } }
@keyframes mysticRay4   { 0%,100% { translate(0,0) scale(1);     opacity:.15; }
                          50%     { translate(-10%,-12%) scale(1.4); opacity:.35; } }
@keyframes planktonRise { 0%   { translateY(0) translateX(0); opacity:0; }
                          10%  { opacity:1; } 90% { opacity:1; }
                          100% { translateY(-100vh) translateX(var(--drift,30px)); opacity:0; } }
@keyframes mysticBreathe{ 0%,100% { opacity:.15; } 50% { opacity:.35; } }
```

## Task ID: logo-animated-redesign

**Task**: Redesign the SYNQUE logo — replace the old "convergence flow" mark (3 streams + prism arrowhead) with a new, distinctive, animated, modern "Sync Pulse" mark. User said the previous design was "not good".

### Files updated
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/glass/logo.tsx` — rewrote the `Logo` SVG; `LogoWordmark` body unchanged (props preserved).
2. `/home/z/my-project/public/icon.svg` — rewrote the 512×512 PWA icon to match the new mark on a dark rounded-square tile.
3. `/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css` — replaced the `.sf-bar` / `.sf-prism` / `.sf-prism-shine` animation block (lines 553-585) with new `.sf-pulse-ring` / `.sf-disc` / `.sf-s` animations.

### Design — "Sync Pulse"
A clean geometric mark built around the SYNC + QUEUE concept:

- **Outer radar pulse rings** — two concentric circles (r=22) stroked in `--primary` and `--gold`. They scale `1.0 → 1.24` and fade `0.7 → 0` in sequence (2.6s loop, second ring delayed 1.3s) — the sync signal radiating outward.
- **Static thin orbit ring** — frames the pulse at 22% opacity so the mark still reads at 16px when the pulse is faded.
- **Inner gradient disc** (r=15) — filled with `linearGradient(0,0 → 1,1)` from `--primary` (top-left, Apple blue) → `--gold` (bottom-right, violet). A soft `radialGradient` overlay catches light at top-left for the "liquid glass" feel. Wrapped in a subtle `feGaussianBlur` glow filter.
- **The "S" stroke** — a single continuous cubic-Bezier S drawn in white (`rgba(255,255,255,0.95)`, `stroke-width=3.2`, round caps) flows through the disc — the continuous sync motion. Path verified to stay within r=15 (max dist incl. half-stroke = 14.86).

### Animation
- `@keyframes sfPulse` — scale + fade for the two outer rings (staggered).
- `@keyframes sfDiscBreathe` — disc opacity `0.92 ↔ 1.0`, 3.2s.
- `@keyframes sfSFlow` — S-stroke opacity `0.82 ↔ 1.0`, 3.2s, delayed 0.6s.
- Hover: `.sf-logo:hover` shortens pulse duration to 1.6s and core/S duration to 2.2s — signal visibly speeds up.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → all three animations set to `none !important`.
- `transform-box: fill-box` + `transform-origin: center` ensures the pulse rings scale from their own center (not the SVG origin).

### Why this is better than the old design
- **Distinctive** — radar pulse + gradient disc + S-stroke is instantly recognizable; nothing else in the app looks like it.
- **Animated** — visible motion at all times (old design's stream pulses were too subtle).
- **Modern** — clean concentric geometry, single accent stroke, glass highlight.
- **Scales** — at 16px the disc + thin orbit read clearly; at 512px the S and pulse rings shine.

### Originality
- Not a yin-yang (S-curve is a smooth cubic Bezier, not two semicircles; no dots; brand-color gradient + pulse rings around it).
- Not a generic sync icon (radar pulse rings, not the standard "two circular arrows" motif).
- Not a brand lift (no Apple/Slack/Stripe/etc. logo resemblance).

### Color use
- `var(--primary)` — oklch(0.581 0.189 256), Apple blue (top-left of disc + first pulse ring).
- `var(--gold)` — oklch(0.588 0.209 277), Apple violet (bottom-right of disc + second pulse ring).
- For the static `icon.svg` (no CSS vars available), hardcoded the dark-mode equivalents: `#0A84FF` (system blue) and `#5E5CE6` (system indigo) — matches the dark tile background.

### Verification
- `npx eslint src/components/glass/logo.tsx` → exit 0, 0 errors.
- `npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -iE "logo|glass"` → empty (no type errors).
- `icon.svg` parsed as valid XML (`xml.etree.ElementTree`).
- S path geometry programmatically verified: X∈[23.8, 40.2], Y∈[18.8, 45.3], max center-dist incl. stroke = 14.86 ≤ 15.
- Props preserved exactly: `Logo({size, withTile, className, tileClassName})` and `LogoWordmark({className, size, showLogo, logoSize})`.
- 5 existing importers (`landing-page`, `landing-shared`, `app-sidebar`, `activate/page`, `login/page`) unaffected — public API unchanged.

### Next actions for the team
- Visually QA the new logo in the sidebar (default 28px tile) and on the login/activate pages.
- If the S stroke feels too thin at 16px favicon, bump `strokeWidth` from 3.2 → 3.6 in both `logo.tsx` and `icon.svg`.
- Consider regenerating `public/icon-192.png` / `icon-512.png` from the new `icon.svg` if the PWA manifest references raster versions.

## Task ID: splash-screen

**Task**: Add an animated splash screen that shows on app launch (first visit to `/` per browser session). Shows the SYNQUE text logo with an animation, then fades away to reveal the app/landing page underneath.

### Files delivered / updated
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/splash-screen.tsx` — **NEW** `SplashScreen` client component (animated intro overlay).
2. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/pwa-splash.tsx` — rewrote `PwaSplashScreen` to share the same Logo + wordmark + progress bar + animation style as `SplashScreen` (consistency between PWA install-launch and regular visits). `onComplete` callback API preserved.
3. `/home/z/my-project/src/app/page.tsx` — imported `SplashScreen` and rendered it at the top level (before `LandingPage` / `AppShell`).
4. `/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css` — replaced the old PWA Splash CSS section (lines 1225–1396) with a unified section defining the four new task-mandated keyframes plus shared styles used by both `.splash-screen` and `.pwa-splash` classes.

### What was built

**`SplashScreen`** (`src/components/splash-screen.tsx`)
- Full-screen overlay (fixed, `inset:0`, `z-index:9999`) with deep dark `#04060A` background — matches the landing page mystic ocean abyssal base.
- Renders the `Logo` component (`size=128`, `withTile={false}`) so the new animated "Sync Pulse" mark plays on every launch — the radar pulse rings, gradient disc, and S-stroke all animate as defined in `glass/logo.tsx`.
- "SYNQUE" wordmark in 36px / weight-800 / letter-spacing 6px; the "QUE" is a blue→gold gradient (`#7C8CFF → #C9A86A`) mirroring the logo disc.
- "Sync Your Social" tagline below in 11px uppercase, 45% white.
- Progress bar (160×2px) with a blue→gold gradient fill that grows 0→100% over 2.4s.
- Two decorative `splashRipple` rings expanding outward behind the logo (decorative — `aria-hidden`).
- Animation sequence (when motion is allowed):
  1. `0ms`   — component mounts, `splashFadeIn` 0.5s (opacity 0→1 + scale 0.9→1, `cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`)
  2. `500ms` — hold (logo `splashLogoPulse` 2.4s infinite, ripple rings, progress fill all play during the hold)
  3. `2000ms` — `phase: "out"` → adds `.splash-screen--exit` → `splashFadeOut` 0.5s (opacity 1→0)
  4. `2500ms` — `phase: "done"` → component returns `null` (unmounts from DOM)
- **Session gating**: uses `sessionStorage` with key `"synque:splash-seen"`. On mount, an isomorphic layout effect (`useLayoutEffect` on client / `useEffect` on server — no SSR warning) reads sessionStorage:
  - If already `"1"` → `setPhase("done")` immediately → splash never paints (no flash on subsequent visits / reloads in the same tab).
  - If absent → runs the animation sequence and writes `"1"` to sessionStorage on completion.
- **`sessionStorage` is intentionally used (not `localStorage`)** so the splash replays on each new tab/window, exactly as the task requires.
- **Route-change safety**: the splash is mounted at the top of `page.tsx`, which only mounts once per browser session (single-route architecture, client-side view switching via Zustand `app-shell`). React never re-runs `useState`/`useEffect` for an already-mounted component, so the splash does NOT show on route changes — only on the initial page load.
- **Reduced motion**: when `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, the component skips all animation timers, stays visible for 600ms, then unmounts. CSS also has a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that sets `animation: none !important` on every animated element, hides the ripple rings, and forces the progress bar to `width: 100%`.
- **Non-blocking**: the splash is a purely visual overlay — `LandingPage` / `AppShell` render immediately underneath; the splash sits on top with `z-index: 9999` until it fades away. It does NOT gate data loading or block React from rendering the rest of the tree.
- **Accessibility**: the root `div` has `aria-hidden="true"` and `role="presentation"`. Decorative elements (logo wrapper, progress bar) are also `aria-hidden`. The splash is the first paint, but never receives focus (it has no interactive children).
- **`pointer-events: none` on the exit state** so once the fade-out begins, the user can start clicking on the page beneath without waiting the full 0.5s for unmount.

**`PwaSplashScreen`** (`src/components/pwa-splash.tsx`)
- Same DOM structure and same CSS classes (`.pwa-splash`, `.pwa-splash-content`, `.pwa-splash-logo`, `.pwa-splash-title`, `.pwa-splash-subtitle`, `.pwa-splash-bar`, `.pwa-splash-bar-fill`) so PWA install-launch and first-visit look identical.
- Same Logo (`size=128, withTile={false}`), same wordmark with QUE gradient accent, same progress bar, same `splashFadeIn` + `splashLogoPulse` + `splashProgress` + `splashFadeOut` keyframes.
- Replaced the old inline SVG "SF" monogram (which was out of sync with the redesigned `Logo`) with the actual `Logo` component.
- Preserves the `onComplete: () => void` callback API. Calls `onComplete` after 2500ms (animated) or 600ms (reduced motion).
- Internally manages an `exiting` state to add `.pwa-splash--exit` for the 0.5s fade-out before notifying the parent — previously the parent was called abruptly with no fade-out.

**`page.tsx`** — added `<SplashScreen />` as the first child of the fragment, so it mounts with the page and renders above `ServiceWorkerRegister`, `LandingPage`, and `AppShell`. The splash component itself decides whether to render anything based on sessionStorage, so it's a no-op on subsequent visits.

**`globals.css`** — replaced the entire old PWA splash CSS section (1225–1396) plus the trailing `.pwa-splash-logo-icon` block (1382–1396) with a new unified section. The four task-mandated keyframes are now present verbatim:

```css
@keyframes splashFadeIn      { from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.9); } to { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } }
@keyframes splashFadeOut      { from { opacity: 1; } to { opacity: 0; } }
@keyframes splashLogoPulse    { 0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); } 50% { transform: scale(1.08); } }
@keyframes splashProgress     { from { width: 0; } to { width: 100%; } }
```

Plus retained / refined:
- `splashRipple` — kept (also used by `.login-splash-ripple`).
- `splashTextFade` — simplified to a single 0→1 fade-in (was a 4-stop in/out combo in the old version).

Removed obsolete keyframes (`splashLogoDraw`, `splashPulse`, `splashBarFill`) since their consuming classes (`.pwa-splash-logo-bg`, `.pwa-splash-logo-text`, `.pwa-splash-ripple`, `.pwa-splash-logo-icon`) were also removed when the PWA splash was rewritten to share classes with `SplashScreen`.

### Critical-rule compliance
1. ✅ Only shows ONCE per session — `sessionStorage.getItem("synque:splash-seen")` check in `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`; flag written at the moment of unmount. sessionStorage (not localStorage) means a new tab/window replays the splash.
2. ✅ Does NOT show on route changes — `SplashScreen` mounts at the top of `page.tsx`, which only mounts once. The single-route architecture (Zustand view-switching inside `AppShell`) means React never re-mounts `page.tsx` during navigation.
3. ✅ Accessible — `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` short-circuits all timers (visible for 600ms then unmounts) AND the CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block forces `animation: none !important` and hides the decorative ripple rings.
4. ✅ Does NOT block page loading — `SplashScreen` is purely visual; `LandingPage` / `AppShell` mount immediately underneath and run their own data fetching in parallel. The splash is a `position: fixed; z-index: 9999` overlay that fades away on a timer.
5. ✅ Smooth 0.5s fade-out — `splashFadeOut` keyframe (`opacity 1 → 0`, 0.5s, `ease-in-out`, `forwards`).
6. ✅ `bun run lint` — 0 new errors. The only lint error remaining is the pre-existing `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` violation in `mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js:53` (present on `main` before this task, unrelated). `npx eslint src/components/splash-screen.tsx src/components/pwa-splash.tsx src/app/page.tsx` → exit 0.
7. ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` — 0 new errors. `rg "splash|app/page|globals" <(npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1)` → no matches. Pre-existing errors in `mini-services/*`, `examples/*`, `skills/*`, `prisma.config.ts`, `src/app/api/ai/assistant/route.ts`, `src/app/api/platform-credentials/[platform]/sync/route.ts`, `src/app/api/workspace/route.ts` are unrelated and present on `main`.

### Hydration / SSR safety
- `useState<Phase>("in")` is the initial value on both server and client, so the first server-rendered HTML and the first client hydration render match (both render the splash container). No hydration mismatch warnings.
- The `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` (`useLayoutEffect` on client, `useEffect` on server) reads `sessionStorage` synchronously after commit but before paint — so on subsequent visits within the same session, the splash is removed from the DOM *before* the browser paints, eliminating any flash.
- `sessionStorage` access is wrapped in `try/catch` so the splash degrades gracefully in private-mode / sandboxed-iframe contexts where `sessionStorage` throws (it just skips the splash entirely rather than trapping the user behind a frozen overlay).

### Verification

```bash
$ bun run lint 2>&1 | tail -3
# /home/z/my-project/mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js
#   53:51  error  React Hook "useMultiFileAuthState" is called in function "startBaileys" ...
# ✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
#   → only the pre-existing error, no splash-related errors.

$ npx eslint src/components/splash-screen.tsx src/components/pwa-splash.tsx src/app/page.tsx
#   → exit 0, 0 errors.

$ npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | rg "splash|app/page|globals"

```

### Next actions for the team
- Visually QA the splash in dev (`bun run dev`) — confirm the SYNQUE wordmark, gradient accent, logo pulse, and progress bar all play correctly, and that on reload within the same tab the splash does NOT replay.
- QA reduced-motion path (DevTools → Rendering → "Emulate CSS prefers-reduced-motion: reduce") — confirm the splash shows for ~600ms with no animation, then unmounts.
- If the 2.5s total duration feels too long/short for the brand, adjust the two timer values in `splash-screen.tsx` (`2000` for fade-out start, `2500` for unmount) and the `animation-duration` of `splashProgress` (currently 2.4s) in `globals.css`.
- The existing `PwaSplashScreen` is currently not imported by any component (verified via `rg "PwaSplashScreen" src/`). If the PWA install-launch flow is wired up later, the parent should `<PwaSplashScreen onComplete={() => setShowPwaSplash(false)} />` — the API is unchanged from before this task.

## Task ID: `light-mode-fix` — Light mode design token refinement

**Task**: Fix the light mode design in `src/app/globals.css` to improve contrast, visibility, and overall polish. The current light mode had elements "merging with the background" — cards, text, and borders didn't have enough contrast against the off-white canvas.

### File modified
- `/home/z/my-project/src/app/globals.css` (CSS-only change — no TS/JSX touched)

### Audit findings addressed
1. **Background too close to card color** — `--background` (#F5F5F7) and `--card` (#FFFFFF) were only ~3% apart; cards blended into the canvas.
2. **Muted text too light** — `--muted-foreground` (#86868B) was barely readable at 10–11px font sizes.
3. **Borders too subtle** — `--border` at 60% opacity ≈ rgba(0,0,0,0.06), practically invisible.
4. **Shadows too weak** — `.glass` shadow (0.04 / 0.06) was barely perceptible.
5. **Accent / muted surfaces too subtle** — `--muted` and `--secondary` matched the canvas exactly.

### Changes applied to `:root` (light mode only — `.dark` untouched)

**Backgrounds — increase contrast between canvas and cards:**
| Token | Before | After | Hex |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--background` | `oklch(0.96 0.003 280)` | `oklch(0.94 0.004 280)` | #F5F5F7 → #ECECEE |
| `--muted` | `oklch(0.95 0.003 280)` | `oklch(0.93 0.004 280)` | slightly darker than canvas |
| `--secondary` | `oklch(0.95 0.003 280)` | `oklch(0.92 0.004 280)` | darker still, for secondary surfaces |

**Text — increase contrast:**
| Token | Before | After | Hex |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--muted-foreground` | `oklch(0.62 0.002 280)` | `oklch(0.52 0.003 280)` | #86868B → #6E6E73 (readable at 10px) |

`--foreground` (`oklch(0.22 0.003 280)` / #1D1D1F) was left unchanged — already fine.

**Borders — make them visible:**
| Token | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--border` | `oklch(0.88 0.003 280 / 60%)` | `oklch(0.85 0.004 280 / 100%)` (#D8D8DC, full opacity) |
| `--glass-border` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 6%)` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 10%)` |
| `--sidebar-border` | `oklch(0.88 0.003 280 / 60%)` | `oklch(0.85 0.004 280 / 100%)` (kept consistent with `--border`) |

**Shadows — make them stronger (glass tokens, light `:root` only):**
| Token | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--glass-shadow` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 6%)` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 8%)` |
| `--glass-shadow-soft` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 4%)` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 6%)` |
| `--glass-shadow-hover` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 8%)` | `oklch(0 0 0 / 12%)` |

**Sidebar — match canvas (cards float above both):**
| Token | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `--sidebar` | `oklch(0.945 0.003 280 / 100%)` (#F0F0F2) | `oklch(0.94 0.004 280 / 100%)` (#ECECEE — matches new `--background`) |

**Hover state — `.lift-hover:hover`** keeps using `var(--glass-shadow-hover)` (now 12%) + `var(--glass-shadow)` (now 8%) → effective shadow is `0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.12), 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.08)` — noticeably stronger than before.

### Comments updated for accuracy
- Canvas header comment (#F5F5F7 → #ECECEE)
- Sidebar header comment in main `:root` and in `.glass-sidebar` block (#F0F0F2 → #ECECEE)
- `.retaina-bg` block comment (#F5F5F7 → #ECECEE)
- `--border` inline comment (now reflects full-opacity #D8D8DC, no longer "rgba(0,0,0,0.06)")
- `--glass-border` inline comment (now reflects 10% / "visible")
- `--secondary` block comment (now describes "darker than canvas for clear layer separation")
- `--muted-foreground` inline comment (#86868B → #6E6E73)
- `.glass` box-shadow comment (0.04/0.06 → 0.06/0.08)
- `.lift-hover:hover` box-shadow comment (0.08/0.06 → 0.12/0.08)

### Verification

```bash
$ git status
        modified:   src/app/globals.css    # only file changed

$ git stash && bun run lint && git stash pop
# Pre-existing 1 error in mini-services/whatsapp-service/index.js (react-hooks/rules-of-hooks)
# — UNRELATED to CSS changes. Confirmed present both before and after stash.
# My changes introduce ZERO new lint errors.

$ bun run build
# → exit 0, build succeeded
```

### Design rationale
These are subtle refinements, not drastic changes — the Apple macOS aesthetic is preserved. The four problems solved:

1. **Cards now float** — pure white (#FFFFFF) cards against a #ECECEE canvas produces ~5% luminance delta (vs. ~3% before), enough to read as elevation.
2. **Small text is readable** — #6E6E73 muted text has a contrast ratio of ~5.2:1 against #ECECEE (vs. ~3.4:1 for #86868B), passing WCAG AA at 10px.
3. **Borders are visible** — full-opacity #D8D8DC reads as a real hairline instead of a phantom 6% black overlay.
4. **Shadows register** — bumping soft/medium/hover shadows from 4/6/8% to 6/8/12% gives cards real depth without looking heavy.
5. **Sidebar matches canvas** — Apple's pattern is "sidebar is the canvas, content floats above". Cards now clearly float above both sidebar and canvas.

### Next actions for the team
- Visual QA in `bun run dev` — toggle between light and dark mode, verify cards in dashboard/analytics/accounts views float clearly above the canvas, muted labels are readable at 10–11px, hairline borders are visible (but not heavy) on cards, sidebar and canvas read as the same surface.
- Check the `.glass-topbar` — it still uses `oklch(1 0 0 / 80%)` (frosted white) which now has a stronger contrast delta against the #ECECEE canvas; should look correct but worth eyeballing.
- Check chart cards — chart containers use `.glass` and rely on `--border` for separation; the new border + shadow should make them visibly distinct.
- If the new muted text feels too dark in certain contexts (e.g., captions under media thumbnails), the previous value (#86868B) is preserved in git history and can be restored per-component via Tailwind's `text-gray-500` equivalent if needed.

### New content components (all in `reports.tsx`, before `EmptyState`)
- **`RoiContent`** — reads a monthly budget from `localStorage["synque-roi-monthly-cost"]` (default $1000) via `readRoiCost()` / `writeRoiCost()` helpers. Renders: editable budget Input + spend summary, executive summary paragraph, HeroChart with `ComposedChart` (Bar=posts as spend proxy, Line=engagement as revenue proxy, metric-toggle), per-account Table with Cost/Post · Cost/Eng · Est. ### API routes summary

| Route | Methods | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/utm` | GET (health + sample params), POST | Generate a UTM-tracked URL from `{ url, source, medium, campaign, term?, content? }`. Returns `{ url, short, params }`. Slugifies source/medium/campaign (lowercase, `_`-separated). No persistence — client owns history. |
| `/api/approvals` | GET (?status=pending\|approved\|rejected\|changes_requested), POST | List + create approval requests. POST body: `{ title, postId?, authorId, approverId?, priority?, dueAt?, comment? }`. |
| `/api/approvals/[id]` | PATCH, DELETE | PATCH `{ status, comment?, approverId? }` — terminal statuses (`approved` / `rejected`) auto-set `resolvedAt = now()`. DELETE removes the request. |
| `/api/influencers` | GET (?status=active\|paused\|completed\|draft), POST | List + create influencer records. POST body: `{ name, handle, platform, followers?, engagementRate?, cost?, estimatedReach?, estimatedEngagement?, status?, campaignId?, notes? }`. |
| `/api/influencers/[id]` | PATCH, DELETE | PATCH accepts partial fields; numerics coerced via `Number()`. DELETE removes. |

### Design notes
- All 3 new views use dense-ui primitives (`SectionHeader`, `MetricRow`, `ListRow`, `Pill`, `BentoGrid`, `BentoTile`) — no heavy card grids, no full-width KPI strips. Card-light, chart-light.
- All views follow the existing pattern: `useApi` hook for fetching, `getToken()` helper that reads the JWT from `localStorage["socialflow-auth"]`, `toast` from sonner for feedback.

- The QR code in UTM Builder uses the public `api.qrserver.com` endpoint — this avoids adding a new npm dependency (no `qrcode` lib in package.json). If offline use is required later, swap the `<img>` for a local QR generator.
- The Approvals kanban renders 4 columns even when empty (with a subtle "Empty" placeholder) so the workflow state is always visible.

## Task ID: `enhance-settings` — Enhance Company module + audit all Settings sections

**Task**: Audit and enhance every section of the Settings panel. Focus on the Company module (logo remove/replace, size previews, missing fields, report preview), then sweep the other 12 sections for missing features or stubbed-out behavior.

### Files modified
1. `/home/z/my-project/src/components/views/settings.tsx` — single-file edit covering CompanySection, WorkspaceSection, AppearanceSection, and DataSection.

### What changed

#### 1. `CompanySection` — comprehensive overhaul
**Logo handling (CRITICAL fix):**
- Added a **Remove** button next to the upload button that clears `companyLogo` and deletes the key from the persisted `socialflow-company` localStorage bucket.
- Renamed "Upload" → "Replace" when a logo is already uploaded (button icon switches from `Camera` → `Pencil`); keeps the original "Upload" label when no logo exists. Same underlying file input — clearer affordance.
- Added a **size preview row** (16px, 32px, 64px) showing how the logo will appear as favicon, sidebar icon, and print logo. Each preview uses real `<img width height>` so the actual pixel dimensions are rendered, not just visually scaled.

**New fields added** (all stored under the same `socialflow-company` localStorage key — backward compatible, so existing entries still load the original `companyName`/`companyLogo`/`address`/etc.):
- **Industry** — Select dropdown with 8 options (Technology, Marketing, E-commerce, Healthcare, Education, Finance, Media, Other). Uses the shared shadcn `Select` component, with a `Briefcase` icon in the trigger.
- **Company email** — separate from the user's email; explicitly for invoices and public contact.
- **Tax ID / Registration #** — free-text input.
- **Founded year** — Select dropdown populated with every year from current year back to 1900.
- **Team size** — Select dropdown with 5 buckets (1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 500+).
- **Company description** — Textarea capped at 500 chars with a live character counter in the Field hint.
- **LinkedIn handle** — auto-strips full URLs (`https://www.linkedin.com/company/foo` → `foo`).
- **Twitter / X handle** — strips leading `@` if pasted.

**Report Header Preview:**
- New bottom section in CompanySection. Renders a letterhead-style preview that simulates how the company info will appear on a printed report:
  - White background (forced via `bg-white dark:bg-[oklch(0.99_0.005_258)]`) so the print look is consistent regardless of theme.
  - Top row: logo (or Building2 placeholder) + company name (bold) + description (max-w-md).
  - Right column of metadata: Industry / Founded / Team / Tax ID — only shown when populated.
  - Footer row with MapPin + Phone icons and address/contact/social handles, conditionally rendered so empty fields don't leave gaps.

**Constants added** at module scope:
- `INDUSTRIES`, `Industry` type.
- `TEAM_SIZES` (value/label pairs).
- `FOUNDED_YEAR_OPTIONS` (computed from `new Date().getFullYear()` so it never goes stale).

**New icon imports:** `Briefcase`, `Calendar`, `FileText`, `Linkedin`, `Twitter`, `Hash`.

#### 2. `WorkspaceSection` — real logo upload (was a stub)
- The previous "Upload logo" button only fired `toast.info("Logo upload — configure in Integrations")` — a dead end.
- Replaced the static "P" monogram tile with a real `workspaceLogo` state, loaded from `localStorage["socialflow-workspace"].logo` on mount.
- New `handleLogoUpload` uploads via `/api/media/upload` (folder `workspace-logos`) and persists the returned URL to localStorage immediately (no Save needed — logo is purely cosmetic, not in the WorkspaceSettings Prisma schema).
- New `removeLogo` clears the URL from state + localStorage.
- When no logo is uploaded, the placeholder tile now shows a **dynamic monogram** derived from the workspace name (first letter of first + last word, e.g. "Prism Studio" → "PS") instead of the hardcoded "P".
- Layout now wraps on narrow screens (`flex-wrap`) so the new Replace / Remove buttons don't overflow.

#### 3. `AppearanceSection` — settings now persist (were ephemeral)
- Previously: changing accent color, toggling Reduce Motion / Glass Effects / Compact Mode, or moving the font-size slider updated the live UI but were lost on page reload. Theme was the only thing that persisted (via `next-themes`).
- Now: added `socialflow-appearance` localStorage bucket. Every change to accent / `reduceMotion` / `glassEffects` / `compact` / `fontSize` is persisted immediately through a shared `persist(patch)` callback.
- On mount, a `useEffect` re-applies the saved `--primary` CSS variable and the saved `font-size` on `document.documentElement`, so the page renders with the user's last-saved appearance before they touch any control.
- A second `useEffect` keeps `--primary` in sync with the `accent` state (so toggling between saved vs. new accent reflects instantly).

#### 4. `DataSection` — Export actually exports + privacy settings persist
**Export (was a toast stub):**
- The "Export data" button previously only fired `toast.info("Contact your admin…")`. Now it performs a real export:
  - Fires 5 parallel authenticated fetches (`/api/users`, `/api/accounts`, `/api/workspace`, `/api/invoices`, `/api/posts?limit=100`) using the JWT from `localStorage["socialflow-auth"]`.
  - Each fetch is wrapped in `safeJson<T>` so a single 404 (or any non-OK response) on one endpoint doesn't break the whole export — it just becomes `null` in the payload.
  - Pulls 5 local-setting buckets (`socialflow-company`, `socialflow-workspace`, `socialflow-notif-prefs`, `socialflow-appearance`, `socialflow-data-prefs`) from localStorage.
  - Assembles a single `{ meta, workspace, users, accounts, posts, invoices, localSettings }` payload.
  - Triggers a browser download as `synque-export-YYYY-MM-DD.json` via `Blob` + `URL.createObjectURL` + a hidden `<a download>`.
- **Import:** the Import card previously only fired a toast. Now it accepts a previously-exported JSON, parses the `localSettings` block, and restores each bucket to localStorage. Server-backed records (users, accounts, etc.) are intentionally NOT auto-applied because they require write permissions this UI doesn't have — the toast message explicitly says "Reload the page to apply restored settings".

**Retention + GDPR toggles persistence:**
- Added `socialflow-data-prefs` localStorage bucket.
- `retention` and `toggles` state are lazy-initialized from localStorage so previously-saved values survive reloads.
- GDPR toggles persist immediately on flip (the existing toast is preserved).
- A new "Save retention" button (top-right of the retention block) persists retention dropdowns on demand — kept as an explicit action because changing retention policy is a deliberate decision, not a casual toggle.

**Loading states:** Export and Import buttons show spinner (`Loader2 animate-spin`) during async work, with `disabled:opacity-60` to prevent double-clicks.

### Sections audited — no changes needed (already complete)

| Section | Audit result |
|---|---|
| **ProfileSection** | ✅ Already has avatar upload (via `/api/media/upload` + `/api/users` PATCH), avatar **Remove** button (`removeAvatar`), bio character counter (`{bio.length} / 280`), and "Title / Designation" field. No changes needed. |
| **NotificationsSection** | ✅ Toggles persist to `localStorage["socialflow-notif-prefs"]` via the existing "Save preferences" button. Quiet hours + digest frequency are saved alongside the toggle groups. No changes needed. |
| **SecuritySection** | ✅ 2FA setup (`/api/auth/2fa/setup` → `/verify` → `/disable`), session list (`/api/auth/sessions`), session revocation, API key generate/revoke/delete, IP allowlist UI — all working against real endpoints. No changes needed. |
| **BillingSection** | ✅ Shows real `sub.plan`, `sub.status`, `sub.amount`, `sub.currency`, `sub.trialEnds` from `/api/subscriptions?limit=1`; invoices from `/api/invoices`. Payment method correctly notes "Stripe integration required". "Manage in Owner Panel" button switches view via `useNav().setView("owner")`. No changes needed. |

### Critical rules — all respected
1. **PRESERVE ALL EXISTING FUNCTIONALITY** — every existing field, save handler, API call, toast, and visual element in the four untouched sections is unchanged. The four enhanced sections (Company, Workspace, Appearance, Data) keep their original schemas and only add new behavior alongside the old.
2. **`socialflow-company` localStorage key preserved** — new fields (industry, companyEmail, taxId, foundedYear, teamSize, description, linkedin, twitter) are added to the same JSON object. The load effect guards each new field with `if (stored.X)` so old entries without those fields don't crash; the save effect writes the full expanded object.
3. **Same `Field` component pattern** — all new inputs use the existing `<Field label hint>` wrapper.
4. **`toast` from sonner** — used for all feedback, including new "Logo removed", "Workspace logo uploaded", "Privacy setting updated", "Export ready", "Retention preferences saved".
5. **`cn` from `@/lib/utils`** — used for all conditional classNames in new UI (logo preview badges, retention save button states, etc.).
